I ground rights in sentience, so a being that can suffer holds moral weight in proportion to its sentience, and full negative rights above its class threshold, whatever its species. Science increasingly supports this (Sentience Determination), and that gradient is why fish and crustaceans are covered (bivalves end with aquaculture for consistency).

Whether a being is sentient is determined by the best available scientific consensus (Axiom 5). Under Axiom 2, any being with first-order subjective experience is a rights-bearer, so innocent animals of every kind, including fish and insects, receive sentience protections. Within that protection, moral weight is applied on a sliding scale. It rises with the strength of the evidence for subjective experience and with the richness of that experience, so mammals, birds, cephalopods, and decapod crustaceans weigh more heavily than most fish, and fish more heavily than insects. Everyday accidental harm cannot be policed, so enforcement targets deliberate, unnecessary killing: stepping on a bug is not the target, exterminating a hive for fun is. Where killing animals of any class cannot be avoided in lawful activity, as in harvesting, pest control, construction, and shipping, the duty is to use the least-harmful method that works. Failing to use it should be punished, and incidental kills from lawful activity should carry no criminal liability. Placement on the scale is revised as the evidence changes, and artificial systems are assessed by the same standard.

The law ought to fix the sentience classes in statute, with an expert sentience board that revises a species' placement only on the best available scientific consensus (Axiom 5). A revision applies only to acts committed after it takes effect. The high class would cover all mammals and birds, including rats, mice, and pigeons, and all cephalopod molluscs, such as octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish. Fish would be placed species by species on the evidence for each: a species with strong evidence of pain experience would sit in the high class, and the rest would sit in the lower class until the evidence places them higher. Decapod crustaceans, such as crabs, lobsters, and crayfish, would sit in the high class. Shrimp and prawns span many species, so they would be placed species by species, like fish. Insects would sit on the lowest, precautionary tier. Bivalves are likely not sentient, so they sit in no class and killing one carries no fine; farming them still ends with aquaculture for consistency, not as a sentience claim. Penalties would follow the class as set out above, and deliberately killing an animal on the lowest tier would carry a small fine. The fine would generally go unenforced in practice, because no one can police every insect swatted. The fine would stand anyway, because the law ought to state what is owed to every being that may be sentient, whether or not each breach is caught.

Pest status does not demote a species. Rats, mice, pigeons, and every other high-class animal would stay in the high class. When a high-class pest population occupies a dwelling, food store, or medical facility in a way that foreseeably spreads pathogens or destroys necessary stores, lethal control of that occupying population would be self-defense or defense of rights under the infestation rule in Hunting, Fishing, Pets, and Zoos, not a class change and not a hunting license. The least-harmful method that works should be required. Preventive area-wide extermination of high-class animals that are not occupying a qualifying site remains murder.

Bioengineering of animals follows the stance already taken on predation and herbivores (Wild-Animal Predation): genetic modification of animals is carried out only to advance their sentient-rights protections, never to violate them (Energy & Environment, Bioethics, Progress, & Technology).

The 2012 Cambridge Declaration on Consciousness concluded that the weight of evidence indicates humans are not unique in possessing the neurological substrates that generate consciousness. The 2024 New York Declaration on Animal Consciousness found strong scientific support for conscious experience in other mammals and in birds, and at least a realistic possibility of it in all vertebrates, including fishes, and in many invertebrates, such as cephalopods, decapod crustaceans, and insects. The United Kingdom's Animal Welfare (Sentience) Act 2022 extends its protections to all vertebrates other than humans, plus cephalopod molluscs and decapod crustaceans.
New York University – The New York Declaration on Animal Consciousness (2024)
UK Legislation – Animal Welfare (Sentience) Act 2022, section 5
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Consciousness

Predation is a rights violation regardless of moral agency. Agency governs responsibility and forfeiture, not whether a violation occurred: a predator lacks the foresight and voluntary control of an agent, so it does not forfeit its own rights by the kill the way a deliberate agent does, but its victim's rights are violated all the same (Minors and Incompetent Adults). So the response to predation is protection, not punishment: the duty is to the prey, and the predator keeps its own rights. As with an insane human attacker, lethal force is justified when it is needed to stop an attack in progress. Outside that moment the predator is confined or placed in sanctuary rather than killed.

Within U.S. borders, I believe the government has a duty to intervene against predation. Carnivores that prey on innocent animals should be stopped, or, if non-threatening, placed in sanctuary or confinement and fed lab-grown meat for the rest of their lives. Intervention should be phased: predator numbers reduced humanely through fertility control and sanctuary placement, and herbivore numbers managed the same way, so that removing predators does not lead to overpopulation, starvation, or habitat collapse. The duty is bounded: no step is taken that would cause more suffering or more rights violations than it prevents, and the duty uses only tools that pass testing. Each method starts in pilot areas and expands only after a published review shows it causes less suffering than it prevents, so the program grows with the evidence rather than on a budget or a deadline (What works now). A confined predator that remains violent, shows no sign of change, and cannot be helped may be killed as defensive force against a permanent threat, the same rule that governs an insane human attacker (Insanity Defense); it is not punished, because it forfeited nothing. Outside U.S. borders, intervening is a virtue, not a duty, as with all animal protection. Herbivores, which can live without harming other sentient beings, should continue to receive priority in conservation, habitat, and sanctuary policy (Energy & Environment).
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – The Moral Status of Animals
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Moral Responsibility
Cornell LII – 7 U.S.C. § 2132: Definitions
USDA APHIS – Research Facility Annual Report Summary, Fiscal Year 2024
CDC – About Zoonotic Diseases
Francis Crick Memorial Conference – The Cambridge Declaration on Consciousness (2012)
See also: Applications elsewhere · Abolition of Permanent Incarceration and Compelled Labor

I believe full moral agency needs sentience plus intentional action and foresight, and it scales with sophistication. My own motivation rests on the framework's coherence and on Stoic discipline, not moral facts. Forfeiture should be triggered only by a deliberate violation, found by a court and proportional to the act. Responsibility does not wait on the free-will debate and is absent only where agency is absent. I hold that children and incompetent adults keep full rights and that innocents may not be harmed for others' benefit (Normative Ethics).

A being becomes a full moral agent under my framework when it possesses sufficient first-order subjective experience combined with the capacity for intentional action and foresight of consequences. Agency is not binary in all cases. It scales with cognitive and experiential sophistication. Once agency is present, the being can generate duties through voluntary choices (most clearly seen in the responsibility trigger of voluntary procreation) and can forfeit rights through deliberate violations of others’ negative rights. Non-agent sentient beings (e.g., many animals or fetuses) retain moral status through sentience alone but do not bear the same responsibilities.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Agency
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Moral Responsibility
Because the system claims no independent moral facts (Meta-Ethics), moral motivation cannot rely on them. Motivation instead rests on two pillars:
Rational recognition of the framework's coherence and stability as a system for protecting subjective experience.

The personal cultivation of character through Stoicism. The agent chooses to uphold my framework because it is the best available coordination system and because living in accordance with it supports personal flourishing (Stoic Eudaimonism). Enforcement covers those who reject it (Meta-Ethics).
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Moral Motivation

Weakness of will is acknowledged as a persistent human tendency. Knowing the correct action under the prescribed rules does not guarantee performance. Stoic discipline (Stoic Eudaimonism) is the primary countermeasure: training judgment and repeatedly aligning impulse with reasoned principle. The political system concerns itself primarily with outward rights violations rather than inner moral failure, but I do not excuse akrasia: failure to act rightly when one had the capacity remains a personal shortcoming.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Weakness of Will

Humans readily grasp the logic of negative rights and proportional response when my framework is stated clearly. When an agent knowingly and wantonly violates those side-constraints (Normative Ethics), especially through repeated or severe predation that erodes trust, forfeiture of corresponding rights becomes both intelligible and motivating to observers. The psychological force of forfeiture lies in reciprocity and desert: those who refuse to respect the basic negative rights of others cannot claim the full protection of those same rights. This supports decisive enforcement on recognition of the practical necessity of the prescribed rules alone, with no appeal to moral facts (Meta-Ethics).
Christopher Heath Wellman – The Rights Forfeiture Theory of Punishment
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Retributive Justice

Responsibility does not wait on a resolution of the metaphysical free-will debate. An act counts as a knowing, voluntary violation when the agent understood what it was doing, foresaw that it would harm another, and was not physically compelled. Desires, upbringing, temperament, and mental illness shape choices without erasing them. An agent who chose under their influence still chose. This is why a diagnosed condition does not by itself exempt an offender from the penalties set out in Criminal Justice & Security.

Responsibility is absent only where agency itself is absent: a person physically forced by another, a person who could not understand the nature of the act, or a being without the cognitive capacity for agency at all. These are the incompetence cases covered in Minors and Incompetent Adults. Between full agency and none, the question is factual: whether this agent, at this time, knew what they were doing. Incompetence alone would not lead to execution. A person who was completely unaware and incompetent has no agency and would be removed from society, imprisoned or confined, because they are too dangerous to be around. But a person who cannot be changed from incompetence and remains a threat, violent and showing no sign of change, is a threat to society and would not be kept alive merely for the sake of keeping them alive. They deserve to die, as set out in Criminal Justice and Security.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Compatibilism
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Moral Responsibility
See also: Insanity Defense · Murder, Rape, and the Mandatory Death Penalty · Juvenile Offenders · Self-Defense and Defense of Others

I take Stoic eudaimonism as my personal operating system for character: focus on what is within one's control, practice wisdom, courage, justice, and temperance, and keep composure while acting decisively. It supports my rights framework without replacing it.
I adopt Stoic eudaimonism as my personal operating system for character and daily conduct. Key elements I take from it:
Focus only on what is within my control (my judgments, actions, and responses).
Accept external events, including the actions of others and outcomes of politics, without being ruled by them emotionally.
Cultivate the four cardinal virtues as practical guides: wisdom, courage, justice, and temperance.
Treat adversity and the hostility of others as material for practicing virtue rather than as reasons for despair or rage.
Maintain inner composure while still acting decisively in the world.
Flourish through virtue and rational living.

Stoic eudaimonism is not a replacement for my political or inter-personal rights framework. It is the personal discipline that allows me to live and act consistently with that framework without being destroyed by anger, resentment, or attachment to outcomes I cannot fully control.
Marcus Aurelius – Meditations
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Aristotle's Ethics

In my view the state exists to protect negative rights and the security of the community that sustains them, not to equalize outcomes. Authority and law are justified only as far as they secure rights, and law that systematically violates rights loses legitimacy. A community may control its borders and prefer cultural continuity that preserves a high-trust order, and the state owes its first duty to its citizens. I believe forfeiture scales to groups that systematically violate rights, and that politics cannot create virtue or flourishing.

I hold that the legitimate function of the state is the protection of negative rights and the security of the political community that sustains them. The state exists first to prevent and punish violations of life, liberty, and property, and to defend the community against external and internal threats that would destroy the conditions for those rights. It is not primarily an engine for equalizing outcomes, enforcing comprehensive moral visions, or guaranteeing positive goods.
Robert Nozick – Anarchy, State, and Utopia

head: "Don't the sanctuary system and the predation program contradict a minimal state?"
body: No, because "minimal" describes the state's purpose, not its headcount. The state I want does one job: protecting negative rights and the security that sustains them. Extending that job to every sentient being widens who is protected, not what the state does. A night-watchman for every sentient being is still a night-watchman. A minimal state is not a cheap one. Police, courts, and defense are its core, and defense alone costs about $885 billion in fiscal 2026 on CBO's projection (Fiscal Policy). Size should follow the number of rights-holders and the threats to them, not mission creep (Public-Sector Size and Civil Service). What a minimal state refuses is a different kind of job: equalizing outcomes or granting positive rights. Neither program redistributes anything. Each only stops sentient beings from being killed. The sanctuary system is built to end. Breeding stops on day one, so the population can only fall as the animals live out their natural lives. On my middle case the cost falls from about $349 billion in year 1 to $50 billion in year 10, and the levy ends around year 14, once the population is below 1% of its starting animal units and the bonds are repaid (The Sanctuary Levy). It is paid by liquidation proceeds, sanctuary bonds, and a levy capped at 3% and legally dedicated to the animals. General revenue is only a backstop if the closing endowment runs short. The state runs the sanctuaries only through the emergency phase and then hands them to licensed nonprofits (Handover to Nonprofit Operators). After the last animal dies, there is nothing left for the state to run. The predation program shrinks the same way. The duty is immediate, and its first tools end reproduction instead of building a standing force: no breeding of captive predators, fertility control, and sanctuary placement (Wild-Animal Predation). Bioengineering is used only where testing shows it works, and no step may cause more suffering or more rights violations than it prevents. The research should run through private contracts, as government research already does. Herbivore fertility control is a lasting task, but it replaces wildlife management that state agencies already do today, mostly through hunting. Capital punishment is the same kind of job. Courts already try and sentence murderers; my rules make the sentence swift and final, and they need no new agency. Ending death row removes years of housing and appeals from every capital case (Capital Trials and the Abolition of Death Row). Both programs should be reported to the public every year as separate budget lines, with the sanctuary animal-unit count and the predation program's tested results, so anyone can check the cost against what it protects.

head: "Won't the powers needed for borders, crime, and assimilation spread into the economy?"
body: They are built not to. Every power I give the state is tied to a rights violation or a threat to the community's security, and enforcement targets acts, never beliefs or economic outcomes (Political Authority and Coercion). Border and crime powers reach entrants and offenders, not prices, wages, or what a business makes. The limits on the state's economic reach stand on their own: a single flat income tax with a large zero bracket, a balanced budget as the target, no subsidies without taxpayer opt-in, no positive rights to fund, emergency powers that expire on a fixed date, and a Sanctuary Levy with its own end rule (Fiscal Policy). I believe every enforcement program should also carry its own public budget line and a statutory review date, as the sanctuary and predation programs do, so growth in any of them is visible and has to be voted on again.

I believe political authority is justified only insofar as it is necessary to serve the purpose above. Coercive power is a tool, not an intrinsic good. It must remain bounded by the same side-constraints that apply to individuals, except where an agent has forfeited rights through serious violation. I accept expansive state power only when required to suppress recurrent patterns of rights violation or to defend the community against organized threats.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Authority
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Political Legitimacy
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Libertarianism

In my view, justice consists primarily in the reliable protection of negative rights and the impartial application of rules that respect agency and responsibility. A just order secures the conditions under which sentient beings can exercise agency without predation and enforces rights forfeiture against violators. Distributive patterns are not themselves the measure of justice. The protection of side-constraints and the maintenance of a high-trust framework for cooperation are.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Justice
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Distributive Justice
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Libertarianism

head: "Isn't rejecting positive rights cruel to the poor?"
body: No. Rejecting positive rights rejects compelled redistribution as the default, not help. The floor that remains is not a right anyone can claim against others. It is part of the state's security role, since a community where people starve in the street, die untreated at the hospital door, or grow up unable to read cannot keep the order that protects everyone's rights (Purpose of the State). It is a short list of named exceptions, each funded by minimal necessary taxes: emergency shelter and emergency medical care. Basic K-12 funding averaging about $10,000 per child, paid by each state from its general revenue; an earnings-only top-up for low earners, paid only on earned income; and a strictly means-tested last-resort allowance for severe disability and the elderly poor (Welfare and Entitlements, Education). Workers in the industries the government shuts down would get no retraining program. They would find new jobs or apply for sanctuary jobs (Sanctuary Plan). People already on benefits would keep their entitlement through the transition, and current retirees and those within ten years of full retirement age would keep Social Security and Medicare for life, funded by opt-in contributions plus the temporary transition levy (Social Security and Medicare Transition). Beyond the floor, help comes through opt-in programs and private giving (Justice).

I believe group statistics are real evidence and shouldn't be denied, and I also believe every person should be judged on their own values and conduct. Those two hold together only if the line between them is drawn in advance, so this is the rule I apply everywhere I use group data.
What group data may do. Group-level data may set policy-level defaults: priors, where a burden of proof starts, screening thresholds, and where patrols, investigators, and other resources go.

What group data may never do. It should never by itself decide anyone's guilt, punishment, forfeiture of a right, removal, citizenship, or other legal status. Those should turn only on the person's own conduct, proven to the standard each one requires.

Every default is individually rebuttable. Each default should name the evidence that overcomes it, the standard of proof, who carries the burden, who decides, and how a decision is reviewed. The one exception is the hard entry ban on places under grounds A and B (Questionable Compatibility). Where open support for genocidal attacks is that common, screening can't reliably sort the hostile from the rest, so the ban lifts for the whole place, not for one applicant. It takes no right, because no foreigner has a right to enter.

Defaults track values and conduct, never ancestry. A default may rest on a person's beliefs or conduct, or on the laws, rulers, and measured opinion of the place they come from. It should never rest on race or ancestry.

Defaults follow the data. A default built on data should be re-reviewed when the data changes, and at least yearly where the data is polling or a government finding, as my entry lists already are. If the data no longer supports it, the default should lapse.

Private caution is not a ruling on anyone's rights. Wariness based on a pattern, such as crossing the street at night, violates no one's rights. A decision that allocates a job, a home, or insurance is different: it should judge each person on their own record (Race and Diversity).

Economists call using a group average in place of missing information about an individual statistical discrimination (Phelps, 1972). That model shows where the line belongs: the group figure is only a stand-in for what is unknown about the person, so it should carry less weight the more individual evidence there is. When a decision would take something a person holds by right, the state should get that individual evidence and not rely on the stand-in.

head: "How does this apply to the Muslim admission presumption?"
body: Being Muslim, or coming from a listed country, sets where the burden starts, not the outcome. Admission is a privilege, so the default takes no right from anyone. What rebuts it: clear and convincing verified evidence of conduct and record on all five points in Immigration and Borders: the Constitution over religious law, equal rights for women and non-Muslims, freedom to leave the faith, rejection of violence, and a record that can be checked. A declaration or an interview alone never meets it. Who decides: a consular or USCIS officer trained for values vetting, with one review of a denial by a second officer on the written record. The applicant carries the burden throughout. The presumption governs admission only. It never applies to citizens or to residents already admitted, whose conduct alone counts. An applicant of any faith who fails the five points is refused, so the presumption is never the test itself. The country-level presumption is reviewed every year with the list. The presumption for being Muslim rests on what the faith teaches, not on a poll, so I would revisit it only if those mainstream teachings changed.

head: "How does this apply to policing and criminal cases?"
body: Crime data may decide where police go. Hot-spot policing, heavy enforcement in gang and high-crime areas, and investigative priorities all follow where crime clusters. At a checkpoint everyone already passes through, profiles may help decide who gets a second look, alongside random checks. A stop or search of a particular person on the street should rest on that person's own behavior. A conviction should rest only on evidence about the defendant, proven at trial, and a capital outcome also needs objective corroboration such as footage or physical evidence (Evidentiary Standard). A group crime rate is never evidence that a particular defendant did it. Inside a declared emergency, crime data may decide where a sweep happens, but each arrest and on-scene sentence should still rest on that person's own conduct.

head: "How does this apply to the office bar?"
body: The office bar turns on a person's own adherence to an excluded ideology: an open adherent cannot truthfully swear the oath for an authority role (Oath of Office and Perjury). Adherence is defined by something checkable, like a sworn statement or the group's own membership records. Ancestry, nationality, family, or appearance alone never establishes it. For a group with no membership records, adherence is shown by a sworn statement or the person's own public profession of the ideology, never ancestry alone. Group origin, meaning place or faith of origin and never ancestry, sets the lens and intensity of questioning: a high-risk origin means harder scrutiny of doctrine, association, and adherence, not an automatic bar. That is a screening threshold under rule 1, and the bar itself still turns on the person's own adherence under rule 2. Eligibility after leaving returns after a formal renunciation that the group's own process recognizes, with perjury covering lies. For a faith with no central membership body or exit process, such as Islam, the renunciation is a sworn public renunciation, and lying in it is perjury. Someone who swears falsely commits perjury, which has to be proven in a criminal trial on evidence about that person. Passing immigration vetting doesn't lift the bar, because a Muslim who passes vetting is still an adherent.

head: "What about heritable group differences?"
body: Average group differences, including in tested ability and in crime rates, are real, and whether genes contribute to them is unresolved (Intelligence, Race, and Crime). Neither answer would change how an individual is treated. No average tells anything about an individual, so the state should never use race in a decision about a person, and employers, landlords, and insurers should judge each person on their own record. The only exceptions are real sex-based actuarial facts and fitness tests applied the same way to everyone. This is where I part from race realists.

head: "Isn't relying on group statistics politically radioactive?"
body: It is unpopular, not unsound, and critics rely on group statistics too. Disparate-impact law lets a plaintiff challenge a hiring practice by its effect on a group, before anyone proves intent. In Griggs v. Duke Power Co. (1971) the Supreme Court held that the law "proscribes not only overt discrimination but also practices that are fair in form, but discriminatory in operation." If group data counts as evidence when it shows a disparity in hiring, it counts as evidence when it shows a disparity in crime. What I refuse is the step both sides should refuse: letting a group average decide one person's guilt, rights, or status (rule 2 above). To reject my rule, a critic has to hold either that group data is never evidence, which would end disparate-impact law, or that it may decide an individual's fate, which my rule forbids. Cornell LII – Griggs v. Duke Power Co., 401 U.S. 424 (1971)
Edmund S. Phelps, American Economic Review (1972) – The Statistical Theory of Racism and Sexism
Braga et al., Campbell Systematic Reviews – Hot spots policing of small geographic areas effects on crime (2019)

Law is a practical instrument for securing negative rights and coordinating behavior within a political community, and its authority derives from that necessity, not from objective moral truth (Meta-Ethics). Valid law should track responsibility and agency, apply rights forfeiture proportionally, and remain limited in scope. When law systematically violates negative rights or abandons impartial enforcement, it loses legitimacy and may justly be resisted.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Legal Positivism
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – The Nature of Law
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Legal Obligation and Authority

I hold that a political community has the right to maintain its sovereignty and to control its borders. Because high-trust societies better protect negative rights in practice, and that trust rests on shared norms together with impartial enforcement of law, a people may legitimately prefer cultural continuity and selective immigration that preserves the conditions for mutual cooperation and rights-respecting order. Open-ended demographic transformation that erodes those conditions ought to be avoided.

The negative-rights protections a government provides apply to the people it governs. Foreign actors, civilians included, who actively harbor ideologies supporting genocide or ethnic cleansing against a nation have, in effect, forfeited those protections against it. Where people abroad actively foment such ideas, join or support terror groups, or vote in and build new ones such as Hamas, the threatened nation has the right and the duty to deal with that threat and defend its people as it sees fit. This does not mean obliterating the foreign country. It means confronting those actively driving the threat. Harboring such an ideology means acting on it: membership, material support, public calls for genocide, or violence, not belief or speech alone. The test and process are in Hostile conduct, removal, and entry. The security of a nation's people is paramount.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Sovereignty
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Immigration
Robert D. Putnam, Scandinavian Political Studies (2007) – E Pluribus Unum: Diversity and Community in the Twenty-first Century
Dinesen, Schaeffer & Sønderskov, Annual Review of Political Science (2020) – Ethnic Diversity and Social Trust: A Narrative and Meta-Analytical Review

The state retains a primary duty to its own citizens. Alliances, interventions, and international commitments ought to be evaluated according to whether they advance the security and long-term interests of the political community. No foreign tribunal or external authority holds legitimate veto power over decisions necessary for national survival or the protection of citizens’ rights.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Political Realism in International Relations
Hans Morgenthau – Politics Among Nations

head: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: The same logic of rights and forfeiture that applies to individuals scales to political life. Agents or organized groups that systematically violate the negative rights of others, or that seek to subvert the rights-respecting order itself, may be met with decisive force. Reciprocity and the practical necessity of deterrence justify withholding full rights protections from those who reject the basic framework of non-aggression and mutual restraint.
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: I hold that a doctrine is an excluded ideology when its program, as taught by its own authoritative texts and mainstream tradition, calls for state power to strip people of equal negative rights by status (race, religion, sex, class, or leaving the faith), and states acting on it have done so. Nazism, communism, socialism, and Islam meet that test, and they are the only four that meet it today, so Christianity, Judaism, other faiths, and atheism are not barred. I judge Islam by its mainstream legal tradition, which gives non-Muslims and women lesser standing and prescribes death for leaving the faith (The Islamic Faith in Practice). The test is the same for every doctrine, religious or secular, and any doctrine that meets it would fall under the same rules. The United States ought to designate excluded ideologies by constitutional amendment, never by executive declaration. Adherence to an excluded ideology would carry two civic disabilities and nothing more. First, no authority role - elected or appointed public office; law enforcement, military, and intelligence; judges and prosecutors; immigration and other adjudicators; K-12 public curriculum authority: no one holds a negative right to those powers, so this is the government choosing who may wield them, not a punishment, and not a ban on every taxpayer paycheck (Oath of Office and Perjury). Second, no building, rebuilding, expansion, or relocation of places that promote it, which caps them, mosques included, at today's number: an institution built to propagate a doctrine whose program is to strip others of their rights is organized subversion of the rights-respecting order, and the bar would fall on the institution, never on a person's private belief, speech, or home practice. No one would be fined, jailed, removed, or silenced for holding or advocating any view. The two bars protect the people each of these programs would strip of rights from meeting it in a judge, an officer, or a new institution built to spread it.
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

head: The Civilizational Risks: parity and differences among the four excluded ideologies
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: The four are held on the same terms, as Civilizational Risks at the same level, under the two disabilities above: the authority-role bar, applied through the oath those roles require (Oath of Office and Perjury), with ordinary non-authority public jobs left open. And the building bar (Property Rights). The government would condemn all four in its official voice and would give none of them official platforms, public funding, or public honors. Condemnation would punish no one's belief (Cultural Stance). Holding, praising, or advocating any of them should stay legal for everyone under one speech rule: only true threats and incitement to imminent violence are punished (Free Speech and Censorship).
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: They differ in what each program does and in what each builds:
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: Islam stands apart from the other three first in what it is. I hold that Islam is a political ideology whose goal is sharia, the rule of Islamic law: beyond the death penalty for apostasy and the lesser standing of non-Muslims named above, women are second-class citizens under it, bound to obey their husbands and forced to cover themselves. Even in its moderate form, this is widely accepted. In Pew's survey of the world's Muslims, most Muslims across South Asia, Southeast Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, and the Middle East and North Africa favored making sharia the official law of their country, large shares of those supporters backed death for leaving Islam, and in nearly every country surveyed most Muslims said a wife must always obey her husband. These are the answers of ordinary Muslims across whole countries, not of militants (Breadth of support; Women). Several Muslim-majority states make leaving Islam a capital crime (Apostasy). All the main schools of Islamic law require women to veil, and where that law is state law the state enforces it: Iran makes appearing in public without the hijab a crime, and the Taliban's 2024 law makes covering a woman's entire body mandatory and requires her to cover her face (Compulsory covering). Islam is also the only religion among the four. As above, I judge it by its mainstream legal tradition, not by its theology, and Islamism, the movement to make that law the law of the state, is that program in action (Islamism; The Islamic Faith in Practice). Because it alone has a worship component, it alone carries the mosque rules under the building bar: no new mosques, existing ones capped at today's number, and no state support. The household, guest, and school details are set out in Property Rights and Religious Freedom. It is also the only one of the four for which the office bar is a religious test, which Article VI forbids today, so the bar needs the constitutional amendment (Abdul El-Sayed; Article VI question below).
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: Nazism assigns rights by race. Its program became racial law, conquest, and extermination: the Nuremberg Race Laws, the "euthanasia" killings, and the Holocaust (Nazism). The building bar reaches its gathering places and their symbols.
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: Communism abolishes private property by force under one-party rule. Every state that applied it ran forced-labor camps, and several brought famines that killed millions (Communism). The building bar reaches its strongholds, and the state treats its crimes as it treats Nazi crimes in what it teaches, commemorates, honors, and funds, removing existing public honors of communist figures.
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: Socialism here means socialism in its core sense, imposed by force: state or collective ownership of productive property, central planning in place of prices, and compulsory redistribution beyond a minimal floor. Voluntary cooperatives and worker-owned firms competing in markets are not covered, and I judge social democracy, markets with a large welfare state, as too large a compulsory state, not as socialism (Socialism). The building bar reaches places that promote it.
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: Danger and security: the shared danger level is reached in two ways. By violence, Islam is the most dangerous ideology in the world today. By acceptance, communism, carried today mainly through cultural Marxism, is equally insidious and poisonous to civilization by its wide acceptance among the young and in universities (Cultural Marxism). Islam, communism, socialism, and Nazism are monitored through public data and lawful process at that one level (Terrorism and Domestic Extremism). In immigrant values vetting, being Muslim sets where the applicant's burden starts (Immigration and Borders).
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

head: "Doesn't excluding Islam by amendment establish a religion or rank faiths?"
body: No. The amendment does not establish a religion and does not prefer any faith. It bars doctrines that use state power to strip people of equal negative rights, whether religious or secular, under one published test (Excluded ideologies). Islam is named only because it meets that test, the same test that names Nazism, communism, and socialism. The state endorses no religion (Role of Religion in Government). Article VI's ban on religious tests is overridden by that amendment for this disability alone - the office bar for adherents of an excluded ideology - not to prefer another faith (Abdul El-Sayed).
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

head: "Where is the line between an excluded ideology and ordinary religious or political disagreement?"
body: The line is the published test, and a doctrine is excluded only if all four parts hold (Excluded ideologies): Its program is taught by its own authoritative texts and mainstream tradition, not by a fringe. It calls for state power, not private persuasion. It would use that power to strip people of equal negative rights by status: race, religion, sex, class, or leaving the faith. States acting on it have done so. Ordinary disagreement fails at least one part. A party that wants higher or lower taxes, a church that holds its own members to its own rules, or a movement that wants tighter borders may be wrong, but none of them asks the state to strip anyone of equal negative rights by status, so none is touched. Holding, praising, or advocating any doctrine, excluded or not, stays legal. Civic disabilities tied to an ideology are not new to U.S. law. The Immigration and Nationality Act makes any immigrant who "is or has been a member of or affiliated with the Communist or any other totalitarian party" inadmissible, and bars such members from naturalization. What I add is one public test that applies to every doctrine, religious or secular. To show the bar reaches ordinary disagreement, a critic has to name a doctrine that meets all four parts and shouldn't be barred, or show that one of the four I name fails a part. Cornell LII – 8 U.S.C. § 1182(a)(3)(D): Immigrant membership in totalitarian party Cornell LII – 8 U.S.C. § 1424: Prohibition upon the naturalization of persons opposed to government or law, or who favor totalitarian forms of government
sub: Rights, Order, and Forfeiture at Scale

body: Politics cannot create virtue, guarantee flourishing, or eliminate all human conflict. I keep the state's role deliberately narrower: to maintain the external conditions under which individuals can pursue their own ends, including character development and personal flourishing, without being subjected to predation or chaos. Over-extension of political power beyond this function tends to generate new rights violations rather than resolve them.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Liberalism
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Perfectionism in Moral and Political Philosophy
See also: Welfare and Entitlements · Education · Agriculture, Grazing, and Habitat · Social Security and Medicare Transition

I treat corporations as tools, not moral agents. The CEO should answer by default, and the people who authorize rights violations are liable as well. Limited liability ought to stay for ordinary business, but not for deliberate violations, fraud, or knowing extreme risk.

I hold that corporations are legal tools, not moral agents. Rights violations attach to human agents. The CEO should answer by default for the company's crimes, and officers and controlling shareholders who authorized the violation should answer as well (Income-Scaled Fines). Limited liability should stay for ordinary contract and tort; the veil ought to be pierced for deliberate rights violations, fraud, or knowing extreme-risk conduct.
These are individual reported events, not statistics. They illustrate the position and do not measure a trend.

Boeing 737 MAX: Boeing admitted that two of its technical pilots deceived the FAA about MCAS and paid over $2.5 billion under a deferred prosecution agreement after crashes that killed 346 people. U.S. Department of Justice (2021) – Boeing Charged with 737 Max Fraud Conspiracy and Agrees to Pay over $2.5 Billion

Purdue Pharma: the OxyContin maker pleaded guilty to three felony conspiracies, admitting it misled the DEA and paid kickbacks to boost opioid prescriptions. U.S. Department of Justice (2020) – Opioid Manufacturer Purdue Pharma Pleads Guilty to Fraud and Kickback Conspiracies

head: "If a corporation is not a moral agent, how can a company be punished?"
body: The company itself is not punished as a moral wrongdoer. Its assets answer for its debts and torts, and the people named above answer personally. Liability follows the agents, so the people who decided cannot hide behind the legal form.

Agency and responsibility scale to persons, so a corporation cannot itself hold moral guilt, and the CEO would answer by default as the person ultimately responsible for the company, along with those who authorize a violation. Organized groups that systematically violate rights meet decisive force under Rights at Scale in Political Philosophy. U.S. courts already pierce the corporate veil only for serious misconduct, such as fraud or abuse of the corporate form.
Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute – Piercing the Corporate Veil

I believe present agents may not impose extreme, unjustified risk of death or rights destruction on future sentient beings. Debt may fund rights-protection and honored transitions, but it should never fund rights violations or permanent subsidies.

Present agents ought not to impose extreme, unjustified risk of death or rights destruction on future sentient beings. Public debt should not bind future people to fund rights violations or permanent subsidy schemes. Debt for rights-protection and honored transition commitments is acceptable; I prefer pay-as-you-go and opt-in for non-rights spending.

head: "Future people do not exist yet. How can anyone owe them anything?"
body: The duty is a side-constraint on present action, not a debt to a present person. Whoever is sentient when the harm lands holds the same rights as anyone else, so an act set in motion now that destroys those rights later is a violation once it lands, the same as a delayed bomb.

Side-constraints bind across time where the harmed party will be sentient, extending the capital-track extreme-risk rule in Criminal Justice & Security forward in time. The honored-commitments rule already protects current retirees during transition in Social Security and Medicare Transition. GAO projects publicly held debt reaching 123% of the economy in 2036, and reports that net interest spending in FY 2025 exceeded federal spending on national defense.
U.S. Government Accountability Office – America's Fiscal Future
See also: Murder, Rape, and the Mandatory Death Penalty · Social Security and Medicare Transition
I find beauty in clarity, competence, and order. Cultures that reward rights-respecting order, skill, and merit tend to produce works of lasting quality.

Beauty in the fullest sense is found in clarity, competence, and order. These are valuable because they are often the conditions under which sentient beings can live well and exercise agency without constant friction. Rights-respecting order - expressed through law, discipline, high agency, and care - generates a deeper form of beauty that frequently produces visible beauty in objects and environments. Natural visual beauty can exist independently of ethics: nature may be visually striking while remaining ethically indifferent or abominable.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Beauty
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Environmental Aesthetics

A culture that rewards rights-respecting order, high agency, developed skill, and merit tends to produce works of lasting aesthetic quality. A culture that treats all output as equal, or that elevates works primarily for therapeutic or political reasons while neglecting competence and clarity, tends toward aesthetic decline.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Aesthetic Judgment
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – The Definition of Art
I believe purpose is realized through exercising agency with virtue, within my framework's ethical constraints. I accept mortality, and I see legacy as the real impact left behind.

Purpose is not discovered as an objective cosmic fact, nor is it purely invented in a vacuum. It is realized through the consistent exercise of agency in accordance with virtue and the prescribed ethical constraints. A meaningful life is one in which the agent develops character, acts rightly toward other sentient beings, and pursues long-term projects that express competence and care. Stoic Eudaimonism provides the personal aim. Meaning is not a separate mystical property. It is what a well-lived life feels like from the inside when one is meeting the demands of reason and character over time.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – The Meaning of Life
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Stoicism

Mortality is a biological fact, not a moral tragedy that requires supernatural compensation. The appropriate response is clear-eyed acceptance combined with the effort to leave the conditions for other sentient lives better rather than worse. Legacy matters insofar as it reflects actual causal impact - character transmitted, rights-respecting order maintained, useful work left behind - not as a demand for eternal remembrance. Purpose is local and agent-centered: to live well within the constraints, to protect what deserves protection, and to avoid adding unnecessary suffering or chaos.
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Death
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy – Stoicism
I believe the country should put its own citizens first, keep strong borders, and admit immigrants who share Western values and assimilate. Those values, not ethnicity, define who fits.

I give priority to cultural cohesion, high-trust social conditions, national sovereignty, and strong borders. I believe the state's primary duties are to its own citizens and to the long-term continuity of the political community. Immigration should be selective and oriented toward compatibility with the shared Western value structure, judged at the country level and through values vetting of every immigrant, and cultural assimilation is paramount. The border ought to be secured, with lethal force used when necessary. "Western" names a value structure, not an ethnicity, so compatibility is open to anyone of any ancestry who holds those values; being Muslim creates a presumption of failing the values test, rebuttable only by verified individual evidence of conduct and record.

head: "Isn't nationalism just ethnic exclusion?"
body: No. The community is defined by shared values: individual negative rights, liberty, religious freedom with separation of church and state, the rule of law, civic responsibility, and economic opportunity. People of any ethnicity who hold those values are compatible, and being Muslim creates a rebuttable presumption of failing the values test. Compatibility judgments govern admission only; they impose no legal penalty for belief on anyone already within the community; the two civic disabilities for excluded ideologies are not penalties.

head: "Does civilizational nationalism mean barring immigrants by religion?"
body: It can. Being Muslim creates a presumption against admission. So does coming from a country where Islamist movements govern or where survey data (Pew's 2013 survey, fieldwork 2008 to 2012) show majority support for state-enforced religious law. Either presumption can be rebutted only through strict individual values vetting on verified evidence of conduct and record, never on self-declaration alone (Islam and Extremism; Immigration and Borders).

The detailed immigration position is set out in Foreign Policy & International Relations, border enforcement in Border Security and Immigration Enforcement, and the definition of Western compatibility in Western Values and Compatibility. Assimilation and national identity are developed in Cultural & Social Issues, and English as the common civic language reflects Executive Order 14224, which designated English the official language of the United States in 2025.
The White House – Designating English as the Official Language of the United States
See also: Islam and Extremism · Immigration and Borders · Border Security and Immigration Enforcement · Patriotism and National Identity

To me, "Western" means a set of values, not an ethnicity or a place: rights, liberty, religious freedom with church-state separation, rule of law, civic responsibility, and opportunity. Anyone who holds them is compatible, whatever their ancestry. Being Muslim creates a presumption of failing it, which only verified individual evidence can overcome. Compatibility should be judged by country-level presumptions and individual vetting, govern admission only, and penalize no one's belief inside the community. The two civic disabilities for excluded ideologies are not penalties.

"Western" names a value structure rather than an ethnicity or a geography: individual negative rights, liberty, religious freedom with separation of church and state, the rule of law, civic responsibility, and economic opportunity. Compatibility means holding those values. It is judged at the country level on the Questionable Compatibility list: grounds A and B carry a complete entry ban by nationality or origin; grounds C–I and security adds carry a presumption against entry, with no free immigration and only case-by-case admission — including places where Islamist movements govern or where survey data show majority support for state-enforced religious law — and at the individual level through values vetting of every immigrant (see Religion & Secularism and Foreign Policy & International Relations). Compatibility judgments govern admission to the political community; they impose no legal penalty for belief on anyone already within it; the two civic disabilities for excluded ideologies are not penalties (Role of Religion in Government).

My view: Being Muslim creates a presumption of failing the values test. A Muslim applicant is presumed incompatible with the shared Western value structure, and answers in an interview do not overcome that. Only verified evidence of conduct and record does.

head: "Isn't judging cultures as incompatible just prejudice by another name?"
body: The test is about values, and it cuts in both directions. A person who holds these values is compatible whatever their ancestry. A person who rejects them is not, whatever their ancestry. Being Muslim creates a presumption of failing it, which verified individual evidence can overcome. I judge many cultures outside Europe and North America compatible. The judgment is aimed at the value structure and applied to individuals through vetting rather than assumed from origin alone, and it imposes no legal penalty for belief on anyone already in the political community.

head: "How is compatibility with Western values tested in practice?"
body: By objective standards, not by opinion. A lawful non-citizen resident should have to pass the English and civics test used for naturalization within two years of admission, and removal should require a court finding by clear and convincing evidence. Opinions, beliefs, and speech should never be grounds for removal (Removal of Non-Citizen Residents); that rule governs U.S. residents, while foreign security removals follow Hostile conduct, removal, and entry. I would ban entry completely, by nationality or place of origin, from any place whose regime or dominant factions wage or celebrate attacks that target civilians for genocide or ethnic cleansing, or where reliable polling shows 5% or more openly supporting such attacks. The list is reviewed every year, and a place comes off only when open support stays below 1% in consecutive annual reviews and no authority there endorses such attacks. Further grounds for a ban are set out in the list (Hostile conduct, removal, and entry; Questionable Compatibility).

The values in that list are the ones the rest of my framework already depends on. Individual negative rights and liberty are the core of Ethical and Philosophical Framework. Religious freedom with separation of church and state is set out in Religion & Secularism. The rule of law and civic responsibility appear in Authority & Civil Liberties, and economic opportunity in Domestic Policy & Governance. A person who holds these values is compatible whatever their ancestry. A person who rejects them is not, whatever their ancestry.

Because the test is about values, it cuts in both directions, and being Muslim creates a presumption of failing it. I judge many cultures outside Europe and North America compatible. Many legally immigrated Mexican and other Latin American communities are named as examples in Cultural & Social Issues. I judge cultures whose governing norms clash with these values, such as Islamist movements that seek state-enforced religious law, incompatible. That judgment is aimed at the value structure, and it is applied to individuals through vetting rather than assumed from origin alone.

Christianity's historical role is acknowledged as part of how these values developed in the West, while scripture is never mandated (Religion & Secularism). The standard is the values themselves, which a citizen can hold as a Christian, a member of another faith, or an atheist.

Shared values matter because trust is the medium of a rights-respecting order. Robert Putnam found that in the short run, residents of more ethnically diverse U.S. neighborhoods showed lower trust, even of their own group, and less community cooperation, and that successful immigrant societies overcome this by building shared identities. A 2020 meta-analysis of 1,001 estimates from 87 studies found a statistically significant but small negative relationship between ethnic diversity and social trust, stronger for trust in neighbors. A common value structure is the shared identity that lets a diverse society keep its trust.
Robert D. Putnam, Scandinavian Political Studies (2007) – E Pluribus Unum: Diversity and Community in the Twenty-first Century
Dinesen, Schaeffer & Sønderskov, Annual Review of Political Science (2020) – Ethnic Diversity and Social Trust: A Narrative and Meta-Analytical Review
See also: Islam and Extremism · Immigration and Borders · Removal of Non-Citizen Residents and Loss of Citizenship · Role of Religion in Government · Due Process and Rule of Law

I support free markets, a flat tax with a large zero bracket, opt-in welfare, no business subsidies without opt-in, regulation that must justify itself, and balanced budgets with defense first. A flat, time-limited Sanctuary Levy of no more than 3%, on income above $75,000 single or $150,000 joint, should pay for the care of animals freed by the shutdown of animal agriculture and testing.

I want a free-market-leaning economy, with low and simple taxation built on a flat income tax with a large zero bracket. I reject mandatory welfare and large-scale redistribution in favor of an opt-in model. Subsidies to any business or industry should require taxpayer opt-in, industrial policy ought to be minimal and tightly justified, and the burden of proof should rest on every regulation rather than on the people regulated. Budgets should be balanced, with defense the top spending priority. There are two time-limited exceptions to the single flat rate. The first is a 2-point transition surcharge through 2041, all of it to the debt (Taxation). The second is a flat Sanctuary Levy of no more than 3%, on income above $75,000 single or $150,000 joint, for the care of animals freed by the shutdown of animal agriculture and testing. It ends when the sanctuary population falls below 1% of its starting animal units and its bonds are repaid (Sanctuary Plan).

head: "Without mandatory welfare, what happens to people in need?"
body: The welfare model is opt-in, and emergency protections remain, such as emergency shelters and emergency medical care set out in the detailed domestic policy section. What I reject is compulsory redistribution as the default, not help for people in genuine emergencies. The rule protects two people at once: the worker whose wages would otherwise fund programs they never chose, and the person in need, whose floor is funded separately so no opt-in shortfall can remove it (Welfare and Entitlements). If the compulsory part is too small, the gap falls to voluntary giving, which anyone may add to; if it is too large, the excess is taken by force every year from people who did nothing wrong. Some people will get less from the state than today's programs give, and everyone already on Social Security and Medicare is grandfathered for life.

head: "Isn't a flat income tax regressive?"
body: The flat rate would sit on top of a large zero bracket, so the lowest earners would pay no income tax at all, and everyone above it would pay the same rate on income past that bracket. Taxes would stay low and simple and fund only essential functions. In dollar terms the largest cuts go to the highest earners, whose top federal rate falls from today's 37% to the flat 20% (22% through 2041 with the transition surcharge). I accept that on the principle of one rate for everyone (Taxation).

head: "Don't billionaires own almost everything while wages stagnate?"
body: No on both counts as usually stated. The Federal Reserve's Distributional Financial Accounts show high concentration at the top, but not "billionaires own all wealth": the top 0.1% holds on the order of about 14% of household wealth in recent DFA releases, and the rest of the distribution still holds the majority. Real average hourly earnings have risen over the long run, with a sharp real dip in the 2021–22 inflation spike and a recovery since (BLS). Housing and wealth are not owned only by billionaires. I reject wealth taxes and large-scale redistribution anyway on rights grounds (Taxation). The myth correction matters so the debate is about principles, not invented shares. Across countries, more billionaires per person goes with less poverty, not more (Economic System). How the US tax system ranks on progressivity, and what the "billionaires pay 8.2%" figure measures, is in Taxation. Federal Reserve – DFA: Distribution of Household Wealth · BLS – Real average hourly earnings

head: "Why is defense the top spending priority?"
body: The state exists first to protect negative rights and the security of the community that sustains them, including defense against external threats (Political Philosophy). Defense is that core function, so it comes first in a balanced budget.

head: "Does economic nationalism mean heavy tariffs?"
body: No. I treat tariffs as good in theory, as leverage and as protection for strategic industries, and questionable in practice, because studies of the 2018 tariffs found they were passed almost entirely into prices paid by American buyers. American industry should be supported mainly through full expensing, long-run payroll tax cuts as the transition levy steps down, and regulatory relief, and through trade deals in which the United States also exports to each partner (Trade and Economics).

The tax, welfare, and regulatory positions are set out in Domestic Policy & Governance, including Welfare and Entitlements, Infrastructure and Regulation, and Fiscal Policy. The no-subsidy rule is applied to energy in Energy & Environment. The scale of business subsidy the rule removes is visible in agriculture. Direct government payments to U.S. farm producers totaled about $54 billion in 2020, measured in 2024 dollars, much of it pandemic assistance, according to USDA's Economic Research Service.
USDA Economic Research Service – Direct Government payments to U.S. farm producers, 2020–24F
See also: Taxation · Political Philosophy · Trade and Economics · Welfare and Entitlements · Infrastructure and Regulation

I see traditional family life as the preferred default but not a legal mandate. Merit should replace identity politics, speech should be near-absolute, and the government ought to condemn Nazism, communism, socialism, and Islam. Private belief is left alone, but holding those doctrines disqualifies a person from sworn authority roles under the values test.

I prefer the nuclear family and traditional social patterns as the default, without legal mandates for private life; same-sex marriage should be legal, and divorce allowed. I oppose identity politics and DEI frameworks, and people should be treated on merit. Free speech ought to be near-absolute, with narrow exceptions for true threats and incitement to imminent violence. Nazism, communism, socialism, and Islam should be condemned in the government's official voice, with no official platforms, public funding, or public honors. All four are Civilizational Risks at the same level (Terrorism and Domestic Extremism). The criminal law should restrict them only as it restricts any other ideology; as excluded ideologies, Nazism, communism, socialism, and Islam also carry two civic disabilities, which are not penalties.

head: "How can the government condemn an ideology and still protect free speech?"
body: Condemnation is the government speaking for itself. It is not a restriction on anyone else. Citizens keep full freedom to hold and express these views. What they do not get is official endorsement, public funding, or public honors.

head: "Does cultural assimilation mean banning other languages?"
body: No. English is the common language of civic life, and immigrants are expected to learn it as part of joining the shared Western value structure, but private use of any language is free (Language and Assimilation).

The family, speech, and merit positions are set out in Family and Gender, Free Speech and Censorship, Race and Diversity, and LGBTQ+ and Identity Issues. The treatment of Islam is developed in Religion & Secularism. The free speech exceptions track the narrow categories the Supreme Court has recognized; in Brandenburg v. Ohio (1969) the Court held that advocacy may be punished only when directed to inciting or producing imminent lawless action and likely to incite or produce such action.
Cornell LII – Brandenburg v. Ohio (1969)
See also: Language and Assimilation · Family and Gender · Free Speech and Censorship · Race and Diversity · LGBTQ+ and Identity Issues

I would meet crime hard: a mandatory death penalty for murder (including attempted murder), violent rape, child molestation, child rape, kidnapping, human trafficking, large-scale distribution of hard drugs, and giving or selling any hard drug to a minor. forfeiture for repeat offenders; and decisive action against cartels. All of it runs under due process, with police oversight outside emergencies. Belief is never penalized. The two civic disabilities for excluded ideologies are not penalties.

My orientation on crime is hardline. Murder (including attempted murder), violent rape, child molestation, child rape, kidnapping, human trafficking, large-scale distribution of hard drugs, and giving or selling any hard drug to a minor carry a mandatory death penalty under a strict evidentiary standard. Repeat offenders who reach three marks forfeit the right to life, with the victim choosing execution, experimentation, or life with labor (a judge decides when victims disagree or the victim is an animal; where the victim has died, experimentation is the default unless the victim's close family or friends step forward and choose, and it stays the default if they disagree). Sentences for first and second offenses should be greatly increased in length, every custodial sentence served as compelled labor, idle permanent incarceration abolished, and cartels and chronic rights violators should face decisive action. I accept substantial state coercive power as necessary to suppress recurrent predation and disorder, with independent oversight of police. Islam and communism should be treated as civilizational and security threats, monitored only through public data and lawful process, with no legal penalty for belief; the two civic disabilities for excluded ideologies are not penalties.
Embedded block: 6. Criminal Justice & Security#^crime-table →

head: "Doesn't this much state power threaten the innocent?"
body: The power is aimed at those who have violated rights, and outside emergencies it operates under due process: a strict evidentiary standard, compensation when convictions are vacated, and independent auditors of police conduct. Belief alone is never punished. Adherence to an excluded ideology carries only the two civic disabilities in Excluded ideologies.

head: "Isn't hardline crime policy plus nationalism just authoritarianism?"
body: Authoritarianism concentrates power and removes the checks on it. Here the state adds checks alongside the harsh penalties. Emergency powers should be strictly limited (Emergency Powers), every elected office should face the voters every three years (Term Limits), power should be divided and checked (Government Structure and Checks), juries should have to be unanimous (Role of Juries), police should face independent oversight and personal liability, and speech, including speech against the government, should be protected absolutely (Free Speech and Censorship). The state's force falls on those proven to have violated rights, not on dissent or belief.

These positions are set out in Criminal Justice & Security, including Murder, Rape, and the Mandatory Death Penalty, Repeat Offenders and Forfeiture of the Right to Life, Abolition of Permanent Incarceration and Compelled Labor, Police Power and Accountability, and Terrorism and Domestic Extremism; cartel policy abroad is in Foreign Policy & International Relations. Repeat offending is common: among prisoners released from 34 states in 2012, 62% were rearrested within three years and 71% within five, according to the Bureau of Justice Statistics.
Bureau of Justice Statistics (Durose & Antenangeli) – Recidivism of Prisoners Released in 34 States in 2012: A 5-Year Follow-Up Period (2012–2017)
See also: Emergency Powers · Term Limits · Government Structure and Checks · Role of Juries · Free Speech and Censorship

I embrace technology within sentient-rights limits: I support AI and genetics, data should be opt-in, animal testing should be banned, and sentient AI has rights and the same forfeiture rules as everyone else.

I am techno-optimist within sentientist constraints. I support AI, genetic technologies, brain-computer interfaces, and privatized civilian spaceflight, with private innovation preferred and government limited to regulating existential threats, rights violations, and national security. Data trading should be opt-in only. Animal testing should be banned, with experimentation redirected to condemned offenders whose rights are forfeited. Any emergent AI sentience ought to be recognized under the ethical framework and receive full protection, but remain subject to decisive termination if it violates or imminently threatens rights.

head: "Is it consistent to recognize AI sentience and still allow termination?"
body: Yes. The same forfeiture rules apply to every sentient being. A sentient AI holds rights like any other, and like any other it forfeits them if it violates or imminently threatens the rights of others.

head: "How does technology fit the sentientist goals?"
body: I treat lab-grown meat as humanity's best hope for a sentientist world and the replacement path as animal agriculture should be banned, and animal testing should be banned, with experiments done instead on offenders sentenced to the experimentation track (Animal Rights and Sentience Technology; Agriculture, Grazing, and Habitat).

These positions are set out in Bioethics, Progress, & Technology, including AI and Automation, Genetic Engineering and CRISPR, Transhumanism, Animal Rights and Sentience Technology, and Surveillance and Digital Technology. How sentience is determined is set out in Ethical and Philosophical Framework.

I share the classical liberal and libertarian commitment to rights, property, and markets, but I accept far more force against criminals and at the border. I share national conservatism's emphasis on fiscal restraint, a strong military, assimilation, and patriotism, but I base culture on values rather than heritage and keep religion out of government. Grounding rights in sentience sets me apart from all three.

I don't file my views under an existing label. I agree with classical liberalism and libertarianism on negative rights, private property, free markets, and a state limited to protecting people from force and fraud (Ethical and Philosophical Framework; Domestic Policy & Governance). I part from libertarianism in accepting far more coercive power against those who violate rights: the mandatory death penalty (Criminal Justice & Security), strict borders with lethal force when necessary (Foreign Policy & International Relations), and decisive force against organized threats. National conservatism, as most people use the term, means being fiscally conservative, socially traditional, and pro-military, with an emphasis on cultural cohesion and national identity. I share that commitment to fiscal restraint, a strong military, assimilation, patriotism, and national interest in trade (Cultural & Social Issues; Foreign Policy & International Relations). I part from it in three places: I ground the shared culture in a structure of values open to people of any ethnicity rather than in religious or ancestral heritage; church and state ought to stay separate and churches ought to be taxed (Religion & Secularism); and the state ought to recognize same-sex marriage (Cultural & Social Issues). What sets me apart from all three is sentientism: rights rest on sentience rather than species, which extends protection to animals and to any truly sentient artificial being (Ethical and Philosophical Framework).

head: "Isn't this just national conservatism with a libertarian economic policy?"
body: No. The movement's own statement of principles calls for public life rooted in Christianity in nations with a Christian majority and for public support of the traditional family. The government ought to keep church and state separate, tax churches, and recognize same-sex marriage. Grounding rights in sentience, meanwhile, has no counterpart in any of the three traditions.

The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy describes liberalism as a tradition in which liberals accord liberty primacy as a political value, with a presumption in favor of liberty that puts the burden of justification on anyone who would restrict it. That is the same burden I place on regulation (Domestic Policy & Governance). The Encyclopedia describes libertarianism as a family of views built on strong rights of self-ownership and property and a correspondingly minimal state. In everyday usage, national conservatism names a fiscally conservative, socially traditional, pro-military outlook centered on cultural cohesion and national identity, and that everyday sense is the one I mostly share. The national conservative movement's formal Statement of Principles, published in 2022, goes further. It calls for public life rooted in Christianity in nations with a Christian majority and for public support of the traditional family, which is where I part ways. Measured against those definitions, my economic and rights positions sit closest to classical liberalism, my security and immigration positions closest to national conservatism, and my religious and sentientist positions apart from all three.
