Bishops back petition to suspend late-term abortion law (Oct. 2, 2026) · The Boston Pilot – Petition organizers 'very confident' they can pause late-term abortion law (Oct. 16, 2026)

27 Oct 2026: the Repeal 188 campaign says the deadline for collecting new signatures has passed, that certified sheets must reach the Secretary of the Commonwealth by 6 November, that about 50,000 certified signatures are needed to suspend the law, and that it already holds 20,000. No emergency preamble has been reported. Repeal 188 – Help us collect all certified signatures!

6 Nov 2026: On the signature-filing deadline, Gov. Maura Healey filed an emergency preamble with Secretary of the Commonwealth William Galvin declaring Chapter 188 an emergency law, so it took effect immediately and cannot be suspended pending a 2028 referendum. Sam Miele, chair of the Compassionate Care Coalition (Massachusetts Citizens for Life and Massachusetts Family Action), said the group dropped off 113,477 signatures certified by local clerks, above the 37,289 needed to put repeal on the 2028 ballot and the 49,719 that would have been needed to suspend the law. Galvin's office is still reviewing the sheets (typically one to two weeks). Healey wrote that "any further delay in implementing the Act would prolong uncertainty for patients, families, physicians and health care institutions, and risk further harm to the health and safety of women in Massachusetts," and in a Substack post said "at least nine patients" had been denied abortion care in Massachusetts since the law was signed. WBUR / State House News Service – Gov. Healey takes emergency action to block effort to suspend abortion law (2026) · Commonwealth Beacon – Healey move puts abortion law into effect early, relaxing restrictions and teeing up fierce 2028 ballot fight (2026)

What happened (sourced): Before Chapter 188, Massachusetts allowed an abortion at or after 24 weeks only if it was needed to preserve the patient's life or physical or mental health, or for a lethal fetal anomaly or a grave fetal diagnosis incompatible with sustained life outside the uterus, and only in a hospital. Chapter 188 replaces those four reasons with "the professional judgment of the physician," bars any medical review process from overriding that judgment, and drops the hospital requirement, so licensed clinics may perform these abortions. Abortion before 24 weeks and written informed consent are unchanged. It took effect on November 6, 2026, after Governor Healey declared it an emergency law; an ordinary 90-day clock from the August 10 signing would have made it effective November 8. Suspension pending a 2028 referendum is blocked by that preamble; Galvin certification of the filed signatures is still pending for ballot access. Massachusetts Legislature – Chapter 188 of the Acts of 2026

My view: This is the drift described in Abortion and Bioethics. A state that allowed abortion after 24 weeks only for set reasons now leaves it to the physician's judgment, at a stage inside the range where expert estimates place the onset of sentience (~12 weeks to after 24-28 weeks). That is why I believe elective abortion should be banned from conception by constitutional amendment: no one can pin down exactly when sentience starts, and countries that set a week limit keep raising it. The rights claim starts at 12 weeks; the earlier ban is a safeguard, not a claim of full negative rights from conception (Abortion ban (from conception)).
Related: Abortion and Bioethics · Sentience Determination

The specialized terms I use, A to Z, each defined in my own words and linked to where I set it out. Unless a definition is describing a real-world concept, these are terms as I use them in my proposed framework, not current law. Hover over, focus, or tap an underlined term on any page to see its definition.

head: 45 CFR 46 (Common Rule)
body: The federal regulations protecting human research subjects; Subpart C limits research on prisoners to minimal-risk studies and research that may benefit them. "CFR" is the Code of Federal Regulations. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: 60-day restraint
body: The Justice Department's practice of avoiding public enforcement steps against candidates close to an election. I believe it should be a fixed written rule, binding in every case, with an exception only for an immediate threat or evidence about to be lost. (site S3, S13)

head: Abolitionism (animal rights)
body: The animal-rights view, linked to Gary Francione and Tom Regan, that animal use should be ended outright rather than made more humane. I share the goal: I believe animal agriculture, fishing, and animal testing should end on day one. Unlike Francione-style abolitionists, who are nonviolent and anti-carceral, I believe animal killing belongs on the capital track. (standard meaning; site S1, S9)

head: Abolitionist project (Pearce)
body: David Pearce's proposal to use technology to abolish suffering in all sentient life, including suffering caused by predation in the wild. As I use it, it means the future "reordering of nature against predation and suffering," pursued within U.S. borders in phases, with no step that causes more suffering than it prevents, each method expanding beyond pilot areas only after a published review shows it prevents more suffering than it causes. (standard meaning; site S1, S7, S10)

head: Abortion ban from conception
body: The legal rule I support on elective abortion: it should be banned from conception, fixed by constitutional amendment. Sentience remains the moral and rights theory. The rights claim starts at 12 weeks, the earliest point in the published expert range for possible fetal sentience onset (~12 weeks to after 24-28 weeks). Before 12 weeks the ban rests on Axiom 3, which gives a fetus on its way to sentience significant moral weight, and Axiom 5, which errs on the side of consistency where science is unclear: no one can pin down exactly when sentience starts. It is also a safeguard, because countries that set a week limit keep raising it. Denmark and Norway raised their on-request limits from 12 to 18 weeks in 2025, France from 12 to 14 weeks in 2022, and Massachusetts Chapter 188 loosened later-term rules in 2026. The amendment should not move later when onset estimates are revised upward, and it should not be revised by the animal sentience-class board. Rape and life-of-mother exceptions should follow the responsibility and conflicts rules in the Abortion topic. I set this out in Cultural & Social Issues: Abortion and Bioethics. (site S7)

head: ACLED
body: The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project, which tracks protests and political violence; it found campus protests 97% peaceful. (standard meaning)

head: ACRPS
body: The Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies, whose 2023-2024 survey of 8,000 people in 16 Arab countries my S8 uses to place countries on the entry-ban list. (site S8)

head: Actuarial sex facts
body: Sex-based statistics on risk, such as life expectancy or accident rates, used in insurance pricing. I believe this is the one group statistic insurers should be allowed to use. (site S7)

head: Age of criminal responsibility
body: The age below which a child is presumed unable to commit a crime. Many countries fix it by law, commonly between 10 and 14, while many U.S. states set none. I believe there should be no fixed age: a minor's liability should follow the severity of the crime. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Agency
body: Responsibility rests on agency, which scales with cognitive and experiential sophistication; only an agent can generate duties through voluntary choice or forfeit rights through deliberate violation. As I explain in Ethical and Philosophical Framework: Minors and Incompetent Adults. (site S1)

head: Agnostic atheism
body: Not believing in any god (atheism) while holding that the question can't be settled with certainty (agnosticism). I tie mine to burden-of-proof skepticism: a claim needs testable, repeatable proof before I accept it. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: AI preemption
body: Preemption means federal law overrides state law. I believe national AI rules should preempt state law, but by statute passed by Congress, not executive order. (site S10)

head: AI, AGI
body: AI is artificial intelligence. AGI, artificial general intelligence, is AI that matches or exceeds humans across most tasks. (standard meaning)

head: Alaska certification suit
body: The Justice Department's October 2026 lawsuit seeking to hold Alaska's U.S. Senate certification. I grade it Directionally opposed. (site S12)

head: Alien Enemies Act
body: A 1798 law letting the President detain and remove citizens of a hostile nation during a declared war or invasion. The administration invoked it against the Tren de Aragua gang in March 2025; I grade that Directionally aligned. (standard meaning; site S12)

head: AMA and Helsinki codes
body: The American Medical Association's Code of Medical Ethics, which bars physicians from taking part in executions, and the World Medical Association's Declaration of Helsinki, which requires informed consent in research. My S10 calls them private professional rules. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: America First
body: A slogan for putting U.S. interests first in foreign and trade policy, used by the Trump administration. My version: "I stand for America First realism with selective Western imperialism," meaning the United States should prioritize its sovereignty, security, cultural cohesion, and manufacturing strength (S8). (site S8; standard meaning)

head: Amnesty
body: Granting legal status to people living in the country unlawfully. I oppose it. (standard meaning)

head: Anarcho-capitalism
body: The view that the state should be abolished and every service, including law, courts, and defense, supplied by private markets. I use it for Hans-Hermann Hoppe; I want a constitutional republic instead. (standard meaning)

head: Anti-collectivism
body: Opposition to collectivism, the view that the group, class, or state comes before the individual and may direct individual lives and outcomes. I use it for my own politics: I believe rights belong to individuals, and each person should be judged as an individual, never by group. (site home page)

head: Anti-naturalism (sentientist)
body: Here, the rejection of nature as a moral standard, not the metaethical term. In S1 I say nature may be "ethically indifferent or abominable," and in S7 that "Nature needs to be civilized." I use the label only in this sense. (standard meaning; site S1, S7)

head: Anti-totalitarian parity
body: My label for treating the excluded ideologies on the same terms in public memory. I believe the state should officially condemn all four and remove public honors for communist figures, while praising Nazism or communism stays legal. (site S1, S2, S13)

head: Antitrust
body: Law against monopolies and anti-competitive conduct. My view: "big is not illegal." (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Aquaculture and breeding mills
body: Aquaculture is fish and shellfish farming; breeding mills are commercial operations that breed animals, such as dogs, in volume for sale. I believe both should end on day one. (standard meaning; site S9)

head: Assimilationism
body: The view that newcomers should adopt the host society's values and way of life. In my selection order, Western-values fit and assimilation come first and American labor needs second (S8). (standard meaning; site S2, S8)

head: Assisted death
body: A competent adult ending their own life with medical help. I believe it should be allowed, with safeguards. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Atkins v. Virginia (2002)
body: Supreme Court case barring the execution of people with intellectual disability. (standard meaning)

head: Autonomous vehicles rule
body: My rule that a self-driving car's programming should never choose to sacrifice an identified rights-holder. (site S10)

head: Autonomous weapons and space weapons
body: Weapons that can select and strike targets without a human decision, and weapons based in space. I accept autonomous weapons only with human judgment kept, and defensive space weapons only. (site S8)

head: Axioms (S1)
body: The seven numbered principles at the base of my framework in S1, such as Axiom 5 (sentience set by revisable scientific consensus), Axiom 6 (the forfeiture threshold), and Axiom 7 (my system as "a coherent system I choose to endorse and want enforced"). (site S1)

head: Bailouts
body: Government rescues of failing firms or banks with public money. I oppose them. (standard meaning)

head: Basic Law (Germany)
body: Germany's constitution, adopted in 1949. It lets the Federal Constitutional Court ban parties that seek to abolish the democratic order, a model of militant democracy, and Article 102 states, "Capital punishment is abolished." (standard meaning; site S11)

head: Bioconservatism
body: Opposition to human enhancement and to reproductive technologies such as cloning, usually on grounds of human dignity or the value of the natural, as argued by Leon Kass. I am against this camp. (standard meaning)

head: Birthright citizenship
body: Automatic citizenship for anyone born on U.S. soil, under the 14th Amendment as now read. I believe it should end by amendment, going forward only. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: BJS, BLS, CBO
body: Federal statistics and budget agencies: the Bureau of Justice Statistics, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and the Congressional Budget Office. (standard meaning)

head: Body cameras
body: Cameras worn by police and other officers to record their encounters. I want them everywhere, including for ICE. (standard meaning)

head: Brain-computer interfaces
body: Devices that connect the brain directly to a computer. I support them with opt-in neural data. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Building bar
body: The bar on building, rebuilding, expanding, or relocating places that promote any of the four excluded ideologies, such as a Nazi gathering place or an Islamic center or school; new mosques are barred outright. "The bar falls on the place and the symbols built into it, never on a person's belief, speech, or home practice" (S3). (site S3)

head: Bulk tracking, facial recognition, and social credit
body: Mass collection of location or other data on the population, automated identification of faces, scoring citizens' behavior, and selling personal data. I believe each should be opt-in, with a high bar for bulk tracking. (site S3)

head: Burden-of-proof skepticism
body: The rule that whoever makes a claim has to prove it, and that an unproven claim should not be believed. It grounds my agnostic atheism. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Capital evidentiary standard
body: Nobody should be executed unless the proof is overwhelming and backed by objective evidence such as video and physical evidence, not just testimony. I lay this out in Criminal Justice & Security: Evidentiary Standard. (site S6)

head: Capital track
body: Crimes I would treat as capital: punished by death (public) or the experimentation track, under the capital evidentiary standard. They include murder, violent rape, child molestation, kidnapping, trafficking, large-scale distribution of hard drugs, giving or selling any hard drug to a minor, cruelty causing lasting injury, and killing a high-class animal. (site S1, S6)

head: Capture of Maduro
body: The January 3, 2026 U.S. military raid that captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro to face drug-trafficking charges. I grade it Aligned. (site S12)

head: Carbon price
body: A tax or cap-and-trade system that charges for carbon emissions. I oppose it. (standard meaning)

head: Carryover basis
body: A rule that an heir takes over the original owner's purchase price for tax purposes, so gains built up before death are taxed when the heir sells. I would use it instead of an estate tax: "tax an heir's inherited gains when the assets are sold." (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Cartels as terrorists
body: My view that drug cartels, and governments that shelter them, are national-security threats to be defeated by force, including war on governments that refuse to cooperate. (site S8)

head: CAT
body: The UN Convention against Torture (1984), ratified by the U.S. in 1994. I believe the U.S. should denounce (withdraw from) it if needed, while keeping the bar on removing any resident to torture in statute. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Catastrophe threshold
body: In standard threshold deontology, the point where the bad consequences of respecting a right become so large (a catastrophe) that the right may be overridden. My threshold is different: it is the agent's own violation of another's rights. (standard meaning)

head: CEO, IQ, ID, U.S., UK, D.C.
body: CEO is chief executive officer; IQ is a standardized intelligence score; ID is identification; U.S. is the United States; UK is the United Kingdom; D.C. is Washington, D.C. (standard meaning)

head: Cephalopods, decapods, bivalves
body: Cephalopods are octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish; decapods are ten-legged crustaceans such as crabs, lobsters, and shrimp; bivalves are two-shelled animals such as clams, oysters, and mussels. I place cephalopods and decapod crustaceans in the high sentience class. Bivalves are likely not sentient and sit in no class; farming them ends with aquaculture for consistency, not as a sentience claim. (standard meaning; site Glossary (Sentience class))

head: Chapter 188 (Massachusetts)
body: A 2026 Massachusetts abortion law that loosened later-term rules. I cite it as an example of limits drifting past 12 weeks, which is why I believe the ban should run from conception. (site Glossary (Abortion ban); site S13)

head: Charter schools
body: Publicly funded schools run independently of the local school district. My per-child funding can follow a child to them. (standard meaning)

head: Child credit and birth credit
body: My proposed family credits: a child credit that doubles from the third child and a birth credit for third and later children, meant to raise births under lower immigration. (site S5)

head: Christian fundamentalism
body: A strict, literal form of Christianity that seeks to shape law and public life by religious teaching. I list it as a Republican break; I believe religion should stay out of government. (standard meaning)

head: Citizen initiative
body: A process that lets voters put a law or constitutional amendment on the ballot by gathering signatures and then decide it by popular vote, as in Switzerland and many U.S. states. I believe states and localities should be free to offer initiatives and referendums, open only to qualified voters, and I support a national initiative. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Civic disabilities
body: My term for the two restrictions on excluded ideologies, the office bar and the building bar. As I write, they "are not penalties": no one is fined, jailed, or silenced for belief. (site S1, S2)

head: Civil asset forfeiture
body: A legal process in which the government seizes property it says is tied to crime through a civil case against the property itself, often without convicting or even charging the owner. Unlike rights forfeiture in my framework, I believe civil forfeiture without conviction should end. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Civil libertarianism
body: Strong protection of individual freedoms, such as privacy, speech, and a fair trial, against the state. "Procedural" stresses safeguards on how the state acts: I believe data, facial recognition, and social credit should be opt-in, and I want body cameras everywhere, a high bar for bulk tracking, and no qualified immunity. (standard meaning; site S3, S6)

head: Civil service merit hiring
body: Hiring government workers by qualification rather than politics. I believe policy roles should serve at the pleasure of elected officials, with fast removal for stated reasons. (site S5)

head: Civilizational nationalism
body: My stance that a nation should protect and pass on a civilization defined by shared Western values, not by ethnicity: "a set of values, not an ethnicity." It drives my immigration selection, which puts values fit and assimilation first (S2, S8). (site S2)

head: Classical liberalism
body: The tradition of limited government, individual rights, free markets, and the rule of law, from Locke and Adam Smith through Milton Friedman. (standard meaning)

head: Clear and convincing evidence
body: A standard of proof higher than "more likely than not" but lower than "beyond a reasonable doubt": the fact must be shown to be highly probable. I would require it for the court finding before a green card or visa holder is removed. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Close-in-age exception
body: A rule, sometimes called a "Romeo and Juliet" clause, that relationships between teenagers close in age are not treated as statutory rape. I believe the age of consent should be 18 with such an exception. (standard meaning; site S6, S7)

head: Coercive conversion methods
body: Forcible or abusive attempts to change a person's sexual orientation or gender identity. I believe they should be banned, while exploratory therapy (talking through a person's feelings without a set goal) should be allowed. (site S7)

head: Coherentism
body: The idea that a set of beliefs is justified by how well its parts fit together, rather than by outside foundations. "Coherentist prescriptivism" is an alternative label for my metaethics: in S1 I prescribe my system "because it is the most coherent and stably consistent framework available." (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Coker v. Georgia (1977)
body: Supreme Court case barring the death penalty for the rape of an adult woman where the victim is not killed. (standard meaning)

head: Colorblind meritocracy
body: The view that law and institutions should not treat people differently by race and should reward individual merit. As I write, "Every offender should be judged as an individual, by the same law," and "race doesn't matter in itself; culture and assimilation do" (S6, S7). (standard meaning; site S6, S7)

head: Combatant track
body: My rule for foreign cartels formally designated as war enemies or Foreign Terrorist Organizations: their property should be seized as enemy property under the laws of war, without a domestic civilian conviction. It is not civil forfeiture, and domestic gangs and undesignated actors would still require a conviction and full due process. (site S3)

head: Companions-in-guilt argument
body: A reply to moral anti-realism: if moral facts are too strange to exist, so are other facts we accept, such as reasons for belief, so the anti-realist argument proves too much. S1 answers this reply in full. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Compelled hard labor
body: My rule that every sentence would include supervised hard labor, with no idle incarceration. (site Glossary (Mark); site S6)

head: Competence qualification
body: The second half of my qualified franchise: passing the voter license test on issues, civics, and laws. (site S3)

head: Competing currencies
body: Letting private or alternative currencies circulate alongside the dollar. (standard meaning)

head: Constitutionalism
body: Government limited by a written constitution and the rule of law, so that officials can't act beyond the powers it grants. (standard meaning)

head: Constructivism (Humean)
body: In metaethics, the view that moral norms are built from the attitudes and choices of agents rather than discovered as outside facts. "Humean" means rooted in human sentiment and choice, after David Hume. S1 calls my view "constructivist in the Humean sense." (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Corporate personhood (agent-liability skepticism)
body: Corporate personhood is the legal treatment of a corporation as a person that can own property, sue, and be sued. My label for this view: corporations are tools, not moral agents, so I believe the CEO should be liable by default, fines should reach up to 4% of global revenue, and the corporate veil should be pierced for deliberate violations. (standard meaning; site S1, S6)

head: Corporate veil
body: The legal separation that normally protects owners and managers from a company's debts and liabilities. "Piercing the veil" means a court holds them personally liable anyway, which I believe should happen for deliberate violations. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Cosmopolitan liberalism
body: Liberalism that gives equal moral weight to every person regardless of nationality, usually favoring open borders and global institutions. Jason Brennan pairs it with epistocracy; I pair epistocracy with civilizational nationalism. (standard meaning)

head: Cultural Marxism
body: As I use it, the critical theory of the Frankfurt School and the strands that grew from it, which recast Marx's class struggle as oppressed groups against oppressors and carry it into culture, institutions, and education. I see it as the main way communism is carried today, and I condemn it because it assigns a person's standing by group instead of by merit or conduct. Critics call the term a conspiracy-theory label; I claim no plot, only published ideas and their spread. (site S2)

head: Cultural traditionalism
body: A preference for traditional family and social forms. Mine is "preference, not mandate": I believe traditional roles are best but should never be mandated. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Data box
body: A collapsible callout I use that collects figures and studies on a topic, including counter-evidence. (site)

head: Day fines (income-scaled fines)
body: Any criminal, civil, or regulatory fine should be set in proportion to the offender's income and wealth. Individuals should pay day fines with no floor or cap, always alongside labor that scales with severity. Corporations should pay a share of global revenue, or their gain from the offense if higher, and the CEO should be personally responsible by default, serving the labor and paying a personal fine; the same should apply to heads of nonprofits and religious groups. I set this out in Criminal Justice & Security: Income-Scaled Fines. (site S6)

head: Day-one bans
body: My position that animal agriculture, fishing, aquaculture, breeding mills, and animal testing should be "banned outright and instantly," with "no lag at all" and no gradual wind-down (S1). (site S1, S9)

head: Death row
body: The years-long wait between a death sentence and execution. I want 30-day capital trials and same-day execution, with no death row. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Debt brake
body: An automatic rule I would adopt that would raise the temporary income surcharge when debt runs above its legislated path, be suspended in recessions, and force spending cuts if it stays on. I lay this out in Domestic Policy & Governance: Fiscal Policy and Taxation. (site S5)

head: Deceptive candidacies
body: Candidates entered mainly to mislead voters or split the vote. I believe the rules for handling them should be fixed before the election (S3 Ballot Access and Deceptive Candidacies). (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Deepfakes
body: AI-generated video, audio, or images that realistically show someone saying or doing something they didn't. I treat deepfakes as speech (S10, S13). (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Default enrollment (opt-out defaults)
body: Signing people up automatically while letting them leave freely. I would use it only where a person protects themselves, as with private disability insurance, retirement accounts, and index accounts, citing Madrian and Shea's finding that 401(k) participation rose from 37% to 86% under automatic enrollment. (site S5, S10)

head: Defensive accelerationism
body: A stance, often called "d/acc," that favors fast technological progress while giving priority to defensive technologies against catastrophic risk. It fits my view on AI: pro-AI, with AI regulated as an existential risk and a defensive AGI prepared (S10). (standard meaning)

head: DEI
body: Diversity, equity, and inclusion: programs that give weight to group identity in hiring, admissions, and training. I believe in no quotas or DEI. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Deontology
body: Ethics built on duties and rights that may not be violated, rather than on producing the best outcomes. Its main rival is utilitarianism. (standard meaning)

head: Desert
body: Desert means punishment matched to what the offender earned by the crime, regardless of whether it deters. As I explain in Criminal Justice & Security: Deterrence and the Justification for Capital Punishment. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Deterrence
body: Justifying punishment by its power to discourage future crime. I do not ground punishment in deterrence; I ground it in desert, incapacitation, and forfeiture. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Directional (transactional) independent
body: A voter with no party identity who backs whichever side moves policy most in their direction. My homepage calls my support "a cost analysis," and S11 says "No modern political party aligns with my entire system." (site homepage, S11)

head: Disparate impact
body: The legal rule, from Griggs v. Duke Power Co. (1971) and Title VII, that a neutral practice causing a disparate impact by race, sex, or another protected trait is unlawful unless the employer shows it is job-related and a business necessity. I believe disparate-impact liability should be repealed. (site S7)

head: Displacement trigger (BLS trigger)
body: My rule for AI job loss: after four straight quarters with the BLS labor share at least 3 points below its ten-year average and the prime-age employment-to-population ratio at least 2 points below its level three years earlier, the tax on capital income would rise from 15% to the 20% flat rate, then by a surcharge of up to 5 points after eight quarters, never above 25% including the transition surcharge and the Sanctuary Levy. Each step reverses when the measures recover for four quarters. (site S10)

head: Distributive justice (patterned principles)
body: The question of how a society's goods should be shared. Robert Nozick contrasted patterned principles, such as "to each according to need," with historical ones that ask only whether holdings were justly acquired and transferred. I hold that distributive patterns are not themselves the measure of justice. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Dominant-party state
body: A state that holds elections but where one party wins every time and governs for decades, as the People's Action Party has in Singapore since 1959. I want an epistocratic republic, not a dominant-party state. (standard meaning)

head: Double jeopardy
body: The Fifth Amendment rule that a person can't be tried twice for the same offense after an acquittal or conviction. My retrial-after-nullification rule departs from it, which I acknowledge (S3). (standard meaning; site S3)

head: DSA
body: Democratic Socialists of America, a left-wing political organization. (standard meaning)

head: Due process
body: The constitutional guarantee, in the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments, that government cannot take life, liberty, or property without fair legal procedure: notice, a hearing, and an impartial judge. I believe maximal penalties should always come with strict due process. (standard meaning)

head: Duty to retreat
body: A rule in some U.S. states that a person must retreat, if they safely can, before using deadly force in self-defense outside the home; "stand your ground" laws remove it. I believe people should be free to defend themselves or others anywhere, with no duty to retreat. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Earnings-only top-up
body: Under my tax plan, low earners would receive a top-up built into the flat tax's zero bracket: a negative income tax paid only on earned income, never for not working. I set this out in Domestic Policy & Governance: Welfare and Entitlements. (site S5)

head: East Potomac golf closure
body: The Park Service's 2026 move to close the public golf course at East Potomac Park in Washington for redevelopment, now paused by a court order. I grade it Directionally opposed. (site S12)

head: Eco-modernism
body: Environmentalism that relies on technology, growth, and dense energy sources like nuclear power to shrink human impact, instead of cutting consumption. Mine is "reliability first, no mandates, nuclear yes." (standard meaning; site S9)

head: Economic nationalism
body: Using tariffs, mandates, and industrial policy to build up domestic industry. I prefer tax and regulatory relief to tariffs and mandates. (standard meaning)

head: Eighth Amendment
body: The part of the U.S. Constitution that bans "cruel and unusual punishments" and excessive bail and fines. I believe it should be amended or abolished. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: EITC and CTC
body: The Earned Income Tax Credit (a refundable credit for low- and moderate-income workers) and the Child Tax Credit (a per-child credit). I believe the earnings-only top-up should replace both. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: El Salvador-style sweeps
body: Mass arrests of gang members of the kind Nayib Bukele's government carried out in El Salvador under a state of exception from 2022. I believe they should be allowed only inside a declared, time-limited emergency. (site S3, S6, S13)

head: Electoral College
body: The system where states' electors, not the national popular vote, choose the President. I would keep it, with electors chosen by ranked choice. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Emergency on-scene sentencing
body: My position that inside a declared, time-limited emergency, police or military could sentence on the spot. The capital standard, body cameras, and later review would still apply, and an officer whose sentence is not supported would be charged with murder. (site S3, S6)

head: Emergency powers and sunset clauses
body: Emergency powers are special powers a government claims in a crisis; a sunset clause makes a law or power expire on a set date unless renewed. I believe emergencies should be necessary, narrow, temporary, and expire automatically unless the legislature renews them. (standard meaning; site S3, S12)

head: Empiricism (fallibilist)
body: Empiricism holds that knowledge comes from experience and observation. Fallibilism adds that any belief, however well supported, could be wrong and stays open to revision, as with my rule that sentience classes be set by scientific consensus and be revisable (Axiom 5). (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Energy emergency and D.C. Guard deployment
body: The national energy emergency declared by Executive Order 14156 in January 2025 and renewed by the President, and the National Guard deployment in Washington, D.C. I fault both for open-ended renewals. (site S12)

head: Epistemology
body: The study of knowledge: what counts as evidence and when a belief is justified. (standard meaning)

head: Epistocracy
body: "Epistocracy means rule by the knowledgeable." The term is Jason Brennan's. In my system the vote would go to citizens who meet a stake qualification and a competence qualification. (site Glossary; site S3)

head: Epistocratic republic
body: The constitutional republic I support, with a qualified (restricted) franchise, also called a limited democracy rather than a full democracy. Epistocracy means rule by the knowledgeable. Elections, ranked-choice voting, and the Constitution would stay, and the vote should go to citizens who meet a stake qualification, the net fiscal voting bar, and a competence qualification, the voter license test on issues, civics, and laws. I lay this out in Authority & Civil Liberties: Epistocratic Republic and Qualified Franchise. (site S3)

head: ESA "harm" rule (Endangered Species Act)
body: The Endangered Species Act. Its regulatory definition of "harm," which since 1981 covered habitat damage that actually kills or injures listed wildlife, was rescinded effective September 14, 2026. I grade that Opposed. (site S12)

head: ESA (education savings account)
body: An education savings account: state money put into an account parents can spend on private school and other approved education costs. Not the same as the Endangered Species Act. I oppose them. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Estate, wealth, VAT, and sales taxes
body: An estate tax is levied on what a person leaves at death; a wealth tax on total net worth each year; a VAT (value-added tax) and a sales tax on purchases. I believe none should exist at any level of government. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: ET
body: Eastern Time (U.S.), the time zone I use for all times here. (standard meaning)

head: Ethnonationalism
body: Nationalism that defines the nation by shared ancestry or ethnicity. My test is about values and open to any ancestry. (standard meaning)

head: Eudaimonism (Stoic)
body: Ethics aimed at eudaimonia, a flourishing life lived through virtue. The Stoic version ties flourishing to virtue, composure, and accepting what one can't control. I use it for personal character only, not for politics. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Evidentialism
body: The rule that belief should match the evidence. My standard in S1: "Proof here means testable, repeatable evidence or reasoning that others can check." (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Evolutionary debunking
body: The argument (Sharon Street, Richard Joyce) that evolution shaped our moral beliefs for survival rather than truth, which undercuts the claim that they track objective moral facts. It is one of my three arguments for anti-realism in S1. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Ex post facto
body: Punishing an act that was legal when it was done. I believe no one should be punished for animal killings before the ban. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Excluded ideologies
body: The four ideologies my proposed constitutional amendment names: Nazism, communism, socialism, and Islam, held on the same terms. I believe their adherents should be barred from sworn authority roles (the office bar) and that places promoting them should be capped (the building bar). No one would be fined, jailed, removed, or silenced for holding or advocating any view. (site S1; site Glossary (Office bar))

head: Executive discretion over federal property
body: My view that the President may decide on monuments and improvements on property the executive already controls, preferably privately or opt-in funded, but that this discretion "is not a power to take new land, spend money Congress has not appropriated, or go beyond the laws that authorize the executive." (site S5, S12)

head: Existential risk
body: A risk that could cause human extinction or permanently and drastically curtail humanity's future, such as misaligned advanced AI or an engineered pandemic. I believe regulation should be limited to research that creates existential risk. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Experimentation track
body: A sentence for offenders who have forfeited the right to life (the capital tier or three marks): instead of execution, they would be used as research subjects in place of animals. I believe the victim should choose between execution and experimentation; where the victim is dead, the default is the experimentation track unless the victim's close family or friends step forward and choose, and it stays the default if they disagree; where there is no single victim, the judge should choose and may not refuse. Harm outside the sentence, such as guard abuse unrelated to a study, should still be punished. (site S6, S10)

head: Expressivism
body: The view that moral statements express attitudes such as approval or disapproval rather than describe facts. S1 says my view has "an expressive element." (standard meaning; site S1)

head: FDA consent rules
body: Food and Drug Administration rules requiring informed consent for clinical trials of drugs and devices. (standard meaning)

head: Fed (Federal Reserve)
body: The U.S. central bank. I believe in a single price-stability rule, no bailouts, competing currencies, no gold standard, and governors removable only for cause. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Federalism
body: Dividing power between the national government and the states. Mine puts defense, borders, and immigration at the federal level and schools at the local level. (standard meaning)

head: Felony and misdemeanor
body: As I would define them, a felony is any offense worth two or more marks, or any capital-tier crime. A misdemeanor is any offense worth one mark or a fine without a mark. As I write in Criminal Justice & Security: Repeat Offenders and Forfeiture of the Right to Life. (site S6)

head: FISA 702
body: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which lets agencies collect communications of foreigners abroad from U.S. providers without a warrant and sweeps in Americans' messages. S3 cites a 2022 FISA Court finding of more than 278,000 noncompliant FBI queries. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Fiscal conservatism
body: A politics of low taxes, limited spending, and balanced budgets. (standard meaning)

head: Fixed-term labor track
body: The fixed-term labor track, as I would set it, is the lesser tier, one or two marks, served for a term the judge should set in proportion to the harm, with a known end date. I set this out in Criminal Justice & Security: Abolition of Permanent Incarceration and Compelled Labor. (site S6)

head: Flag-burning prosecution
body: The August 2025 executive order directing prosecution tied to flag burning. I grade it Opposed because I believe only true threats and incitement should be punishable. (site S12)

head: Flat tax
body: A single income-tax rate for everyone above an exempt amount. Mine is 20% above the zero bracket, with 15% on capital income. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Flood-insurance cap
body: The federal flood insurance program's legal cap of 18% on most yearly premium increases. I believe it should be removed so owners bear the risk of where they build. (standard meaning; site S9)

head: Floor (minimal welfare floor)
body: The minimal provision I would fund from taxes: emergency shelter and emergency medical care, about $10,000 per child for K-12, the earnings-only top-up, and the last-resort allowance. It is "not a right anyone can claim" but part of the state's security role (S1). (site S1, S5)

head: Ford v. Wainwright (1986)
body: Supreme Court case barring the execution of people who are insane at the time of execution. (standard meaning)

head: Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO)
body: A foreign group the U.S. Secretary of State formally designates as terrorist under the Immigration and Nationality Act; giving it material support becomes a federal crime, and its U.S. assets can be blocked. I believe designated foreign cartels should be treated as war enemies. (standard meaning; site S3, S8)

head: Forfeiture (rights forfeiture)
body: In my framework, forfeiture should be triggered only when an agent crosses the threshold set in Axiom 6: violating another's negative rights through force or fraud, or directly imposing a severe, non-consensual risk of serious harm. I set this out in Ethical and Philosophical Framework: Axioms. (site S1)

head: Frankfurt School (critical theory)
body: A circle of Marxist thinkers at the Institute for Social Research in Frankfurt, founded in 1923, including Max Horkheimer, Theodor Adorno, and Herbert Marcuse. Their critical theory, as Horkheimer defined it in 1937, aims not at knowledge for its own sake but at changing society. (standard meaning; site S2)

head: Free-market capitalism
body: An economic system in which property is privately owned and prices, production, and trade are set by voluntary exchange rather than by the state. I support it, with regulation that has to justify itself and no business subsidies without opt-in. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Free-market environmentalism
body: Protecting the environment through property rights, markets, and liability for harm, rather than through mandates and subsidies. I treat pollution as a rights violation that the polluter pays for. (standard meaning; site S9)

head: Free-speech near-absolutism
body: Protecting nearly all speech from legal penalty. I believe only true threats and incitement should be punishable, and hate speech should be legal. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Friedmanite
body: In the tradition of economist Milton Friedman: free markets, a negative income tax in place of many welfare programs, and money managed by a fixed rule. (standard meaning)

head: Full expensing
body: Letting businesses deduct the full cost of equipment and other investments in the year they buy them, rather than spreading it over years. I support it now. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Full retirement age
body: The age at which Social Security pays unreduced benefits, 67 for people born in 1960 or later. (standard meaning)

head: Fusionism
body: The postwar American conservative blend, associated with Frank Meyer, of free-market liberty, traditional values, and anti-communism. It is one of the traditions closest to my view. (standard meaning)

head: Futurism
body: As I use it, an outlook that welcomes and plans for a future reshaped by technology, such as AI, genetic enhancement, and lab-grown meat. It is not the early-20th-century Italian art movement of the same name. (site home page)

head: Gain-of-function research
body: Research that makes pathogens more transmissible or dangerous to study them. I believe it should be regulated as an existential risk. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Gender-critical
body: The view that sex is biological and can't be changed, and that law should rest on sex rather than gender identity. My S7 definition: "A man is an adult human male and a woman is an adult human female." (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Gene drives
body: A genetic technique that spreads a chosen trait through a wild population much faster than normal inheritance. (standard meaning)

head: Geneva IV Art. 49
body: Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention (1949), which bars an occupying power from forcibly transferring or deporting protected civilians out of occupied territory, or moving its own civilians in. I acknowledge my West Bank removals conflict with it. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Geneva limits on POW labor
body: The Third Geneva Convention lets captors put prisoners of war to work only under limits: paid, safe, non-military work, and never officers by compulsion. I believe POWs a tribunal finds to have fought should be open to compelled labor beyond those limits. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Gifted tracks
body: Separate, faster classes for high-ability students. I believe every school system should be required to offer them. (site S5)

head: Global South
body: A broad term for the developing countries of Africa, Latin America, and much of Asia, used in place of "Third World." I believe ties with them should serve U.S. interests and help move supply chains away from China. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Gold Card
body: Executive Order 14351's expedited immigrant-visa path for a $1 million gift to the Department of Commerce. I grade it Directionally opposed because I believe admission should go by values and vetting, not wealth. (site S12)

head: Gold standard
body: Tying a currency's value to a fixed amount of gold. I don't support it. (standard meaning)

head: GOP
body: "Grand Old Party," the U.S. Republican Party. (standard meaning)

head: Grave tier
body: In my framework, the grave tier would cover grave abuse that does not cause lasting injury; it would count as three marks at once: execution, experimentation, or life with labor, as the victim chooses. I lay this out in Criminal Justice & Security: Abolition of Permanent Incarceration and Compelled Labor. (site S6)

head: Green card
body: U.S. lawful permanent residence. I believe green-card and visa holders should be removed after a court finding by clear and convincing evidence, for welfare use, failing the civics test, or any crime above a basic infraction. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Greenland agreement
body: The September 2026 agreement among the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland expanding U.S. defense areas in Greenland. I grade it Mixed. (site S12)

head: Greens, Libertarian, and Constitution parties
body: Smaller U.S. parties: the Green Party (environmentalist, left), the Libertarian Party (minimal government), and the Constitution Party (religious conservative). I see the Greens as closest on animals and nothing else. (standard meaning; site S11)

head: Hard drugs
body: Drugs such as heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, and fentanyl, as opposed to marijuana. I believe private use should be legal and large-scale distribution a capital crime, with no commercial market. Smaller transfers fall on lower tiers, and sharing a known, tested dose with a consenting adult is not capital. Giving or selling any hard drug to a minor is capital at any quantity. (standard meaning; site S6, S7)

head: Hard entry ban
body: The top tier of the Questionable Compatibility list: a complete entry ban by nationality or place of origin, with no case-by-case visa path. (site S8)

head: Harm-based limits (greenhouse gases)
body: My rule that greenhouse gases above the natural baseline are pollution and should be governed by limits tied to actual harm, tightening if credible tail risk appears. (site S9)

head: Heckler's veto
body: Silencing a speaker because opponents threaten disruption or violence. I believe the state should protect the event instead. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Herbivorization
body: The proposal, associated with David Pearce, to reengineer predators over time so they no longer kill other animals. I support it through gene drives and fertility control, within U.S. borders, in phases, with no step that causes more suffering than it prevents, each method expanding beyond pilot areas only after a published review shows it prevents more suffering than it causes. (standard meaning; site S1, S7, S10)

head: Hereditarian research
body: Research holding that genetic differences explain part of measured group differences in traits such as IQ. S6 calls whether the ability gap is genetic "unresolved" and lays out both hereditarian and environmental research. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Hijra
body: Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina in 622, which marks year one of the Islamic calendar; the Quran also makes migration a religious duty for believers who are oppressed where they live. As I use it, it also names Islamic expansion through migration and integration, a way of taking over countries from within. (standard meaning; site S4)

head: Horse soring, bear baiting, angling, grazing
body: Soring is deliberately injuring a horse's legs or hooves to exaggerate its gait in shows; bear baiting is hunting bears over food bait; angling is recreational fishing; grazing means livestock grazing on public land. As I write, the administration actions on each are graded Opposed. (site S12)

head: Hostile conduct (loss of civilian protection)
body: My rule that civilian protection should be absolute except for foreign actors who forfeit it by hostile conduct, as a court finds. Individuals found hostile this way, for example in the West Bank, should be forced out. (site S8)

head: Hot-spot policing
body: Concentrating police patrols and enforcement on the small areas, often a few blocks, where much of a city's crime clusters. A Campbell systematic review of 65 studies found small but significant crime reductions. I support it, with fast, harsh crackdowns in gang and high-crime areas. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: ICC and Rome Statute
body: The International Criminal Court in The Hague, created by the 1998 Rome Statute, tries genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. The U.S. is not a party; I oppose any role for it. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: ICCPR
body: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (1966), a UN treaty the U.S. ratified in 1992. It limits the death penalty and bars medical or scientific experimentation without free consent. I believe the U.S. should exit it to protect the experimentation track and new capital offenses. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: ICE
body: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the federal agency that detains and deports people in the country unlawfully. I believe it should be expanded, with body cameras. (standard meaning)

head: In short
body: The one-paragraph summary box at the top of each of my topics. (site)

head: Incapacitation
body: Justifying punishment by stopping the offender from committing more crimes. It is one of my three grounds, with desert and forfeiture. (standard meaning; site S6)

head: Index account
body: A low-cost private investment account that every adult would be enrolled in by default, with a free opt-out and no taxpayer seed. The state should not run or hold the accounts. (site S10)

head: Infestation
body: When a high-class pest population occupies a dwelling, a food store, or a medical facility in a way that foreseeably spreads pathogens or destroys necessary stores. Those three sites only. A food store is a structure used to store food for persons or animals under care — not an open field, and not a general agricultural barn that is not a food store. A qualifying infestation is a clear disease or rights threat: lethal control of the occupying population should be treated as lawful self-defense / defense of rights, with separation or exclusion first where they will work and the least-harmful method should be required. Pest status should not demote the species. Rats, mice, pigeons, and other high-class animals should stay in the high class. Preventive area-wide extermination of high-class animals that are not occupying a qualifying site remains murder. Hunger, nuisance alone, or fear that pests might arrive later is not an infestation. I set this out in Cultural & Social Issues: Hunting, Fishing, Pets, and Zoos and Ethical and Philosophical Framework: Animal Rights and Sentientism. (site S7, S1)

head: Interventionism (foreign policy)
body: A foreign policy willing to use force abroad. One label for mine is interventionism that punishes threats but rejects nation-building. (standard meaning)

head: Investor visas
body: Residence or citizenship granted in exchange for investment or payment. I oppose them; status should never be sold. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: IPCC and FAO
body: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, the UN's climate-science body, and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN, whose figures put animal agriculture at about 12% of human greenhouse-gas emissions (2015 reference year). (standard meaning; site S9)

head: Islam (excluded)
body: Excluded Islam = Islam judged by its mainstream legal tradition, which gives non-Muslims and women lesser standing and prescribes death for leaving the faith. As I write, "Islam is a political ideology whose goal is sharia, the rule of Islamic law," which is why it is the one religion among the four excluded ideologies. That is what the excluded-ideologies amendment I support would bar from office and from building places that promote it (Excluded ideologies). Adherence: something checkable, like a sworn statement or the group's own membership records; ancestry alone never counts. For a group with no membership records, adherence is shown by a sworn statement or the person's own public profession of the ideology, never ancestry alone. Eligibility after leaving returns after a formal renunciation that the group's own process recognizes, with perjury covering lies. For a faith with no central membership body or exit process, such as Islam, the renunciation is a sworn public renunciation, and lying in it is perjury (Oath of Office and Perjury). Not covered: belief, speech, and home practice, which would stay free, and ordinary non-authority public jobs. No other faith meets the test, so Christianity, Judaism, and atheism are not barred. (site S1, S4)

head: Islamism
body: The political project of ruling by Islamic law (sharia), whose jihadist wing pursues the same goal by terror. I condemn Islam itself, not only its political project, as one of the four excluded ideologies. (standard meaning; site S2)

head: IVF, CRISPR, and embryo screening
body: IVF (in vitro fertilization) creates embryos outside the body; embryo screening tests them for genetic conditions before implantation; CRISPR is a gene-editing tool. I support all three, IVF unrestricted. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Jacksonian
body: Walter Russell Mead's name for an American foreign-policy tradition, after Andrew Jackson: fierce against enemies, pro-military, wary of nation-building and international bodies, and usually protective of entitlements and tariffs. My foreign policy is close to it, though I oppose protecting entitlements and broad tariffs. (standard meaning)

head: Jones Act
body: A 1920 law requiring ships that carry goods between U.S. ports to be U.S.-built, -owned, -flagged, and -crewed. I believe the mandate should go. (standard meaning; site S12)

head: Jury nullification
body: When a jury acquits despite the evidence because it believes the law, or applying it in that case, is unjust. Under my S3 rules juries can nullify, but I believe a nullification acquittal in a mandatory-death-penalty case should be open to one retrial before a different jury. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: K-12
body: Kindergarten through 12th grade, meaning primary and secondary school. (standard meaning)

head: Kantian dignity
body: Immanuel Kant's idea that persons have an inner worth and must never be treated merely as means. In S10 I say: "My framework doesn't rest on Kantian dignity. It rests on negative rights, which an agent forfeits by violating them in others." (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Kennedy v. Louisiana (2008)
body: Supreme Court case barring the death penalty for child rape where the victim is not killed. (standard meaning)

head: Lab-grown meat
body: Meat grown from animal cells instead of taken from slaughtered animals, also called cultivated or cultured meat. I see it as the goal and the replacement for animal agriculture, and I believe it should be allowed to compete and scale up even if it can't meet demand at the same cost right away. (standard meaning; site S9, S10)

head: Last-resort allowance
body: A strictly means-tested allowance I would provide for severe disability and the elderly poor, from general revenue under the backstop logic, with fraud enforcement and periodic medical reviews; a narrow exception. I set this out in Domestic Policy & Governance: Welfare and Entitlements. (site S5)

head: Law-firm orders and the Comey firing
body: Executive orders limiting security clearances and federal access for specific law firms, and the 2025 firing of prosecutor Maurene Comey (daughter of former FBI Director James Comey) without stated cause, later ruled unlawful. I grade both Directionally opposed. (site S12)

head: Legislative (prescriptive) anti-realism
body: The label I use for my metaethics: I deny objective moral facts but still prescribe a system and want it enforced, rather than treating all views as equally valid (relativism).

head: Lesser homicide
body: My category for a self-defense killing that went too far but was close to justified, similar to what some U.S. states call imperfect self-defense. The prosecution should have to prove intent, and the judge should set a lighter sentence. (site S6)

head: Liberal counter-jihad
body: A label for secular, socially liberal politicians, such as Pim Fortuyn in the Netherlands, who oppose Islam and Muslim immigration in the name of liberal values like gay rights and women's equality. (standard meaning)

head: Liberal eugenics
body: Nicholas Agar's term for parents freely choosing genetic traits for their children, with no state coercion, as opposed to state-run eugenics. It fits my S10 view that "designer babies are fine if rights are respected after sentience." (standard meaning)

head: Libertarian paternalism
body: Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein's idea, also called "nudge," of steering choices with default settings that people can freely opt out of. It describes my opt-out defaults for retirement accounts, private disability insurance, and index accounts (S5, S10). (standard meaning)

head: Libertarianism
body: A political philosophy that puts individual liberty and property first and keeps state coercion to a minimum. "Nozickian" refers to Robert Nozick's rights-based version. (standard meaning)

head: Licensing (occupational)
body: State permission required to work in a trade or profession. I believe licensing should exist only to prevent real harm. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Life with labor
body: One of the three outcomes a victim may choose once an offender reaches three marks or the grave tier: life under compelled labor instead of execution or experimentation. (site Glossary (Grave tier); site S6)

head: Limited democracy
body: My other name for the epistocratic republic: "a limited democracy rather than a full democracy," because the franchise is restricted to qualified voters. (site S3)

head: MAGA
body: "Make America Great Again," the Trump-aligned political movement. "MAGA restrainers" are the part of it that wants fewer foreign military commitments, such as less aid to Ukraine and no war with Iran. (standard meaning)

head: Mandated choice and presumed consent
body: Presumed consent treats everyone as an organ donor unless they opt out; mandated choice requires everyone to state a yes or no, as when getting a driver's license. I believe in mandated choice, never presumed consent. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Mark
body: In my framework, a mark would be a recorded conviction counted toward the repeat-offender threshold, and every mark would include supervised hard labor. Every mark should require proof beyond reasonable doubt. As I write in Criminal Justice & Security: Repeat Offenders and Forfeiture of the Right to Life. (site S6)

head: Market pronatalism
body: Pronatalism is policy aimed at raising birth rates. Mine uses credits, tax relief, and housing deregulation rather than mandates, with a goal of 2.1 children per woman; "the nation should renew itself through its own families" (S5). (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Medicaid work-requirement grace period
body: An optional "hold harmless" period through June 30, 2027 that federal regulators offered states before enforcing the new Medicaid work requirement. I grade it Directionally opposed. (site S12)

head: Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security
body: Medicaid is joint federal-state health coverage for low-income people; Medicare is federal health insurance mainly for those 65 and older; Social Security pays retirement and disability benefits funded by payroll taxes. I believe Social Security and Medicare should be voluntary for new entrants and kept in full for anyone within 10 years of full retirement age. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Meritocracy
body: A system that awards positions by ability and achievement rather than by group or connections. (standard meaning)

head: Metaethics
body: The study of what moral claims are and whether moral facts exist, as opposed to normative ethics, which asks which acts are right. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Militant democracy
body: Karl Loewenstein's 1937 term for a democracy that legally restricts movements hostile to democracy itself, as Germany's Basic Law allows bans on anti-constitutional parties. It describes my excluded-ideologies amendment, which bans no party and no speech. (standard meaning)

head: Miller v. Alabama (2012)
body: Supreme Court case barring mandatory life without parole for offenders under 18. (standard meaning)

head: Minarchism
body: The view that the state should be limited to a minimal "night-watchman" role of police, courts, and defense. I lean minarchist but would keep a tax-funded floor and K-12 funding. (standard meaning)

head: Minimum wage
body: A legal floor on hourly pay. I want none, state minimums included. (standard meaning)

head: Mixed constitution
body: A government that blends elements of rule by the one, the few, and the many, as Aristotle and later the American founders described. (standard meaning)

head: Money bail and pretrial release
body: Money bail requires a payment to be released before trial, refunded if the defendant shows up to court. I believe defendants should be released before trial by default and money bail abolished. (standard meaning; site S3)

head: Moral anti-realism
body: Moral anti-realism is the view that there are no moral facts that hold independently of what anyone thinks or prescribes. As I explain in Ethical and Philosophical Framework: Moral anti-realism. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Moral realism
body: The view that there are objective moral facts that hold whatever anyone thinks. "Realist replies" are the counterarguments realists make against anti-realism, which S1 answers. (standard meaning)

head: Mosque cap
body: The part of the building bar that would allow no new mosques and cap existing ones at today's number (S1, S3). (site S1, S3)

head: Mothers' exemption
body: My proposed income-tax exemption for mothers: half for mothers of three children and full for mothers of four, part of the family package meant to raise births under lower immigration. (site S5, S3)

head: Mugler v. Kansas (1887)
body: Supreme Court case upholding Kansas's alcohol ban without compensation to a brewer, holding that banning a use harmful to the public is not a taking. My S9 Q&A cites it for the uncompensated Sanctuary Plan transfers. (site S9)

head: Multiculturalism
body: The view or policy that a country should keep several distinct cultures side by side rather than expect newcomers to assimilate. I believe it works only when the cultures share important common values. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Muslim Brotherhood
body: A Sunni movement founded in Egypt in 1928 by Hassan al-Banna that seeks government by Islamic law, with national branches and offshoots, including Hamas, across the Middle East and in the West. I believe the U.S. should designate as a terrorist organization every chapter shown to support terrorism or to organize violence. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Nation-building
body: Using military occupation and aid to rebuild another country's government and institutions. I reject it: I believe the United States should avoid "open-ended nation-building" (S8). (standard meaning; site S8)

head: National conservatism
body: A movement, associated with Yoram Hazony, that stresses national sovereignty, borders, cultural cohesion, and often religion in public life. (standard meaning)

head: National individualism
body: My own label for my politics: rights belong to individuals, with free markets and a minimal, opt-in fiscal state, held within a strong nation defined by shared Western values, firm borders, and assimilation. I believe the state exists to protect negative rights and the security of the community that sustains them. (site home page)

head: National initiative
body: A constitutional amendment I support that would let qualified voters put federal statutes (1% of qualified voters' signatures) and amendments (2%) on the ballot. Only voters who meet the full election stack (ID, the voter license test, net-taxpayer status, no felony bar) may sign and vote, and no initiative can override protected rights. (site S3)

head: NATO
body: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization, the U.S.-European defense alliance. I support it only when it serves U.S. interests. (standard meaning)

head: Nazism and communism
body: Nazism is the racist, totalitarian ideology of Hitler's Germany; communism is the ideology of abolishing private property under one-party rule, as in the Soviet Union and Maoist China. Both are among my four excluded ideologies. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Negative rights
body: Negative rights are side-constraints against interference and harm. As I explain in Ethical and Philosophical Framework: Axioms. (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Negative utilitarianism
body: A form of utilitarianism focused on reducing suffering rather than increasing happiness. David Pearce holds it; I am deontological instead. (standard meaning)

head: NEH
body: The National Endowment for the Humanities, a federal grant agency. Some NEH funds are reserved for the arch, which is why I grade it directional and would prefer private or opt-in money. (standard meaning; site S12)

head: Neoconservatism
body: An American foreign-policy school that favors using U.S. power to spread democracy, including through regime change and nation-building. I reject nation-building and democracy promotion. (standard meaning)

head: Net-taxpayer franchise (net fiscal voting bar)
body: I believe only net taxpayers should vote. A person would count as a net taxpayer for the prior completed tax year when taxes paid exceed personally directed transfers received and income-tax liability is positive. The franchise would track current net contribution, not lifetime payroll history, because the franchise decides other people's money. Also called the net taxpayer voting bar. The full measurement rules — what counts as a transfer received, which taxes count as paid, the tax-filing unit, joint filers, refundable credit cash-outs, the mothers' exemption, grandfathered Social Security and Medicare, and when the bar lifts — I lay out in Authority & Civil Liberties: net fiscal voting bar and in the questions under Voting and Elections. (site S3)

head: NGO grants
body: Government money given to nongovernmental (nonprofit) organizations. I believe grants should end, with contracts for specific services only. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: NIH women's health division
body: Executive Order 14437 (October 2026) directing the National Institutes of Health to create a Women's Health Division. I grade it Directionally opposed because I believe tax-funded research should be limited to defense, biosecurity, and core functions. (site S12)

head: NIT (negative income tax)
body: Milton Friedman's idea of paying people below an income line a share of the gap, shrinking as they earn more, in place of other welfare programs. My earnings-only top-up is a negative income tax paid only on earned income. (standard meaning; site Glossary (Earnings-only top-up))

head: Normative ethics
body: The part of ethics that asks which acts are right or wrong and why, as opposed to metaethics. (standard meaning)

head: Nozickian
body: After Robert Nozick, whose Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) treats rights as side-constraints, defends a minimal state, and rejects distributive patterns as the measure of justice. My rights theory is Nozickian in that sense, with forfeiture and a minimal floor added. (standard meaning; site S1, S3)

head: Nuremberg Code
body: The 1947 research-ethics principles from the Nazi doctors' trial, whose first rule is that "the voluntary consent of the human subject is absolutely essential." I acknowledge my experimentation track conflicts with it. (standard meaning; site S10)

head: Office bar (authority roles)
body: Civic disability I would apply to adherents of an excluded ideology (Nazism, communism, socialism, Islam): they should not be allowed to hold authority roles — elected or appointed public office; law enforcement, military, and intelligence; judges and prosecutors; immigration and other adjudicators who decide status or benefits; K-12 public curriculum authority. Those roles should be sworn. Lying on the oath should be perjury (Oath of Office and Perjury). Not covered: ordinary non-authority taxpayer jobs (accountant, grounds worker, non-adjudicative clerk, and the like). Belief, speech, and home practice would stay free. The separate building bar would cap places that promote an excluded ideology (Property Rights). (site S1, S3, S4)

head: Opt-in (fiscal voluntarism)
body: My rule that welfare, Social Security, Medicare, the public health plan, subsidies, and similar programs should be opt-in. For subsidies, any public money should be "drawn only from taxpayers who opt in to fund it" (S9). (site S5, S9, S10)

head: Organ use from condemned offenders
body: My S10 position that organs from offenders sentenced to death, or at three marks on the execution or experimentation track, should be usable without consent, "under the same logic as the experimentation track," because their rights would be forfeited. (site S10)

head: Outer Space Treaty
body: The 1967 treaty at the base of space law: it bars nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in orbit, bars any nation from claiming the Moon or other celestial bodies, and reserves them for peaceful purposes. I believe it should stay as the civil baseline but be read to allow defense. (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Paid-leave mandate
body: A law requiring employers to pay workers during family or medical leave. I oppose it. (standard meaning)

head: PAP and LDP
body: Singapore's People's Action Party, which has governed since 1959, and Japan's Liberal Democratic Party. Both keep the death penalty. (standard meaning; site S11)

head: Patriots, ECR, ESN
body: Three right-wing groups in the European Parliament: Patriots for Europe, European Conservatives and Reformists, and Europe of Sovereign Nations. (standard meaning)

head: Pattern recognition (pattern realism)
body: My view that noticing real group patterns is reasonable even when a particular person turns out to be harmless, and that statistics shouldn't be denied. Group statistics never become verdicts on individuals; each person is judged on their own values and conduct. (site S6, S7, home page)

head: Pell Grants
body: Federal grants for lower-income undergraduate students that, unlike loans, don't have to be repaid. I would make them opt-in. (standard meaning; site S5)

head: Penal maximalism
body: My label for using the most severe penalties across a wide range of crimes, such as mandatory death and the three-mark rule, all grounded in forfeiture. (site S6)

head: Phenomenal consciousness (first-order sentience)
body: Having subjective experience, meaning there is something it feels like to be that being. "Any being, biological or artificial, that possesses first-order subjective experience is to be treated as a rights-bearer under my framework. Higher-order self-awareness is not required." (site Glossary (Sentience basis); site S1)

head: Police profiling
body: Police using group traits, such as age, sex, or behavior patterns, to decide whom to check. I would allow it only at checkpoints everyone already passes through, to pick who gets a second look, alongside random checks. A stop or search of a particular person on the street should rest on that person's own behavior, and profiling should never decide guilt (Group Statistics and Individual Judgment). (site S1)

head: Polity (politeia)
body: Aristotle's name for the good form of rule by the many: a mixed constitution that blends democracy and oligarchy, with citizenship tied to qualifications. I call my qualified-franchise republic "a modern Aristotelian polity." (standard meaning)

head: Positive rights
body: Claims to be provided something, such as welfare, health care, or housing. In S1 I say: "I reject positive rights." My floor is "not a right anyone can claim." (standard meaning; site S1)

head: POW
body: Prisoner of war. (standard meaning)

head: Precautionary tier
body: The lowest sentience class, for insects. Deliberately killing an animal in it "should carry a small fine." Bivalves are likely not sentient and are not in it, so killing one carries no fine; farming them ends with aquaculture for consistency. (site Glossary (Sentience class))

head: Prescriptivism (universal)
body: R. M. Hare's view that moral statements are prescriptions, like commands, that the speaker must be willing to apply to everyone in relevantly similar cases. S1: my view is "prescriptivist in form, in the tradition of R. M. Hare." (standard meaning; site S1)

head: Preventive force
body: Striking a threat before it can attack, rather than after. I accept it "when it can be done safely." (standard meaning; site S8)

head: Price-stability rule
body: A fixed rule directing the central bank to keep inflation low and steady, rather than giving it broad discretion. (standard meaning)

head: Private vice
body: Activities that mainly affect the person doing them, such as drug use, gambling, prostitution, and adult pornography. I would legalize them for adults. (standard meaning; site S7)

head: Procreative liberty
body: John Robertson's principle that people have a strong liberty interest in deciding whether and how to have children, including through reproductive technology. My S10 views on IVF, embryo screening, gene editing, and cloning sit near it, though mine rest on sentience-based negative rights rather than autonomy alone. (standard meaning)

head: Progressivism
body: A reform movement on the left that seeks wider state action to correct social and economic inequality, often through group-based policy. I call myself non-progressivist: I believe the state should protect rights, not equalize outcomes or judge people by group. (standard meaning)

head: Prop 12 (California)
body: A 2018 California ballot measure setting minimum space rules for egg-laying hens, breeding pigs, and veal calves and banning sales of products that don't meet them. S11 faults the Republican push to override it, since I believe the United States should ban animal agriculture. (standard meaning; site S11)

head: Prop 209 (Bleemer study)
body: California's 1996 measure ending race-based admissions at public universities. Bleemer (2022) found that underrepresented minority applicants then enrolled at less selective colleges, earned fewer degrees, and earned about 5% less; my S7 cites it as counter-evidence and answers that it "does not make the preference just." (site S7)

head: Property exceptions (two)
body: The two cases S3 puts outside my otherwise permanent property right: "one is barred by amendment, and in the other the owners forfeited it." The first is the building bar; the second is the Sanctuary Plan's uncompensated conversion of animal-industry firms. (site S3)

head: Prophylaxis
body: A preventive measure taken before harm happens, rather than punishment after it. In my resolution of the first apparent tension on the home page, the office bars and mosque cap are "prophylaxis, not punishment," protecting the rights order from ideologies hostile to it. (standard meaning; site home page)

head: Proportionality (punishment)
body: The principle that a punishment or defensive response should match the severity of the wrong. In my framework it is applied once, at the forfeiture decision: what is forfeited corresponds to the violation. (standard meaning; site S1, S6)

head: Psychedelic therapy
body: Clinical use of drugs like psilocybin or MDMA alongside therapy. I believe it should be available by prescription. (standard meaning)

head: Punitive civil libertarian
body: Another name I use for my criminal-justice view: a maximal penalty scale combined with strict procedural safeguards.

head: Q&A
body: A collapsible question-and-answer callout I use that answers a likely objection to a position. (site)

head: Qualified franchise
